articles.title: 30-Unit Denny’s Operator Files for Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: 30-Unit Denny’s Operator Files for Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . EYM Diner has locations in Texas and Florida. A 30-unit Denny’s franchisee filed for bankruptcy, extending a series of financial troubles for restaurateur Eduardo Diaz that’s affected his operations across several major chains. EYM Diner of DFW and EYM Diner of Florida, entities based in Texas and Florida, are the latest businesses connected to Diaz to seek bankruptcy protection. Since 2024, affiliated entities have filed for bankruptcy involving Pizza Hut, KFC, and Panera restaurants, resulting in more than 100 closures across those brands. The breakfast chain is now working with existing franchise partners and creditors to transfer as many affected restaurants as possible to new operators. Denny’s says several locations are financially viable, and franchisees within its system have expressed interest in taking them over. “We have spent the past two years working side by side with Mr. Diaz to support the sale of his Denny’s restaurants; that commitment continues. There are viable restaurants in this group, and franchise partners within our system are willing to step in to help secure their future,” Mark Burgess, senior vice president and chief development officer of Denny’s, said in a statement. The company’s involvement predates the filings. According to Burgess, Denny’s has spent two years assisting Diaz with efforts to sell his restaurants, and that work will continue through the bankruptcy proceedings. The goal is to preserve operations at locations that can succeed under different ownership, protecting jobs and maintaining service for customers. Any ownership transfers would need to proceed through the applicable bankruptcy processes and involve coordination with creditors. Denny’s has not announced any completed transactions. “We are working with those partners and other creditors through the necessary processes to transition operations of as many impacted restaurants as possible to experienced operators in our system,” Burgess said. “For the team members whose livelihoods depend on these restaurants and the guests who count on them, continuity matters. That is where our attention and effort remain.” The latest filings add to a difficult stretch for Diaz’s restaurant businesses, which have experienced financial disputes, lawsuits, bankruptcies, and closures across multiple brands. One of the largest cases involved EYM Pizza, which filed for bankruptcy in July 2024 after a legal dispute with Pizza Hut. The franchisee previously operated approximately 140 Pizza Hut restaurants across several states. Pizza Hut sued the operator over alleged contractual violations, unpaid fees, and poor restaurant performance. The bankruptcy ultimately resulted in the sale of 77 Pizza Hut restaurants to six buyers, with approximately 60 other locations closing permanently. Similar difficulties affected EYM Café, Diaz’s former Panera business in the Houston area. The operator, which once controlled 15 bakery-cafés, filed for bankruptcy after Panera terminated its franchise agreements over alleged violations involving royalty payments, food safety standards, and unpaid vendor invoices. EYM Chicken, the group’s KFC business, filed for bankruptcy in 2025 and shuttered dozens of restaurants. In 2023, EYM King of Michigan shuttered all 26 of its Burger King restaurants in the state following a contractual dispute. The latest bankruptcy also arrives as Denny’s works to improve restaurant profitability through its multiyear Project Grand Slam initiative. The strategy targets average unit volumes of $2.5 million, compared with approximately $2 million previously, through restaurant remodels, operational improvements, menu innovation, technology, and additional sales channels. articles.title: HIT Training Launches Hospitality Employer Call To Action As ‘First Job. Future Career.’ Campaign Champions Better Opportunities For The Next Generation.
articles.titleKo: HIT Training Launches Hospitality Employer Call To Action As ‘First Job. Future Career.’ Campaign Champions Better Opportunities For The Next Generation.
articles.originalSummary: With almost one million young people in the UK currently outside education, employment or training, specialist apprenticeship provider HIT Training (part of The Opportunity Provider – TOP), is calling on the hospitality industry to recognise its vital role in helping the next generation into work. The call comes as the company launches its First Job. Future Career. campaign, introducing Commit to Youth – an initiative encouraging employers to make measurable commitments to creating opportunities for young people. And it comes at a time when the Government is preparing to publish the next stage of the Alan Milburn’ Independent Review into Young People and Work, following his interim findings earlier this year. According to the latest Office for National Statistics figures, an estimated 981,000 young people aged 16–24 were not in education, employment or training between April and June 2026. HIT Training emphasises that hospitality is a leading ‘career starter sector’ and plays a vital role in opening doors to employment and developing the next generation of talent. It says the challenge goes beyond offering more entry-level jobs – employers must also ensure young people are given the support, encouragement and career pathways they need to succeed. Importantly, the campaign also highlights the significant financial incentives available to employers taking on young apprentices. Under current Government arrangements in England, eligible apprentices aged 16–24 can have 100% of their training and assessment costs funded, up to the relevant funding limit. Employers who do not pay the apprenticeship levy may also qualify for a £2,000 hiring payment for eligible new apprentices in this age group, while additional incentives are available for Foundation Apprenticeships. Employers can also benefit from relief on National Insurance contributions for apprentices under 25, subject to earnings thresholds. There is also a 16-18 bonus of £1,000 for all employers of apprentices aged 16-18. HIT Training believes greater awareness and take-up of this support could help more businesses overcome some of the financial barriers to investing in the next generation. Mike Worley, Managing Director of HIT Training says: “Hospitality has always been one of Britain’s great career starter sectors. Some of our most successful chefs, hoteliers and hospitality leaders began with relatively modest first jobs, often discovering skills and ambitions they never knew they had. “But with almost a million young people currently outside education, employment or training, we need to ask whether we’re doing enough to give the next generation that same opportunity. “Crucially, a first chance must be a good first chance. It’s not simply about recruiting a young person into a job; it’s about giving them the support, training and confidence to succeed and showing them where that opportunity could lead. “Through our First Job, Future Career – Commit to Youth , we’re asking hospitality employers to move beyond talking about the problem and make practical commitments to creating opportunities. And we’re ready to help them turn those commitments into successful apprenticeships and lasting careers.” The campaign recognises the considerable commercial pressures facing hospitality employers, including rising employment costs and the challenges of recruitment and retention. It also highlights the importance of supporting existing employees to develop and progress. Investing in experienced team members through apprenticeships can strengthen management capability, improve retention and create opportunities for younger people to enter the workforce. Through Commit to Youth , employers are encouraged to create genuine entry opportunities, remove unnecessary barriers to recruitment, consider Foundation and entry apprenticeships, provide appropriate mentoring and support, and establish visible routes for career progression. articles.title: Dino agenda audiência de conciliação sobre escala 6×1 para o próximo dia 10
articles.titleKo: Dino agenda audiência de conciliação sobre escala 6×1 para o próximo dia 10
articles.originalSummary: O ministro Flávio Dino, do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), marcou uma audiência de conciliação para discutir aspectos da implementação da nova jornada de trabalho após o fim da escala 6×1. O encontro será realizado na próxima terça-feira, 10, às 14h. Dino é relator de ações movidas nesta semana pelas confederações do comércio e da indústria . No despacho, publicado nesta quinta-feira, 5, Dino ressaltou que o objetivo da audiência não é o conteúdo da emenda constitucional que acabou com a escala 6×1. “Não se trata de conciliar quanto ao conteúdo da Emenda Constitucional nº 141/2026, que é plenamente constitucional em sua finalidade e cujo mérito não está sujeito a transação. A redução da jornada e a ampliação do repouso semanal não estão em negociação”, destacou. O ministro acrescentou que a audiência vai se concentrar sobre “aspectos de implementação”, matéria que as entidades interessadas reunidas podem equacionar com maior adequação do que decisão judicial proferida sem sua participação. Ele ainda considerou que o prazo de dois meses para o fim da escala 6×1, questionado pelas empresas, “não se revela, a princípio, inviável”. Ele disse que essa avaliação é “preliminar” e poderá ser revista à luz dos dados que forem levados pelos setores econômicos. O ministro ponderou, por outro lado, que as empresas têm razão sobre a “relevância da autonomia privada coletiva” e destacou que a Constituição reconhece as convenções e acordos coletivos e assegura negociações entre empresas e trabalhadores. “Esse reconhecimento conduz ao dever de buscar a solução consensual”, acrescentou. Dino intimou para o encontro as confederações que representam categorias econômicas, as centrais sindicais que representam os trabalhadores, a Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU), as advocacias do Senado e da Câmara e a Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR). Com informações de Estadão Conteúdo (Lavínia Kaucz). Imagem: STF O post Dino agenda audiência de conciliação sobre escala 6×1 para o próximo dia 10 apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Ruby Tuesday Introduces Everyday Fresh Meals Starting at $9.99
articles.titleKo: Ruby Tuesday Introduces Everyday Fresh Meals Starting at $9.99
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Ruby Tuesday has introduced Everyday Fresh Meals: a new value menu offering guests a variety of entrees at four price points starting at $9.99. Available seven days a week, the menu gives guests more flexibility to enjoy Ruby Tuesday favorites at a consistent price. Each meal includes an entree, unlimited trips to The Garden Bar, and a bottomless drink. “Guests shouldn’t have to plan their week around a deal,” says Kevin FitzPatrick, chief marketing officer at Ruby Tuesday. “With Everyday Fresh Meals, we’re making it easier for guests to enjoy their Ruby Tuesday favorites at a consistent price, any day of the week while giving them more flexibility and value whenever they choose to visit.” Everyday Fresh Meal Offerings $9.99: Single American Smashed Burger $11.99: Double American Smashed Burger, Ruby’s Cheeseburger, Big Crispy Chicken Sandwich, or Grilled Chicken Sandwich. $14.99: Deconstructed Chicken Kabobs, Cajun Chicken Pasta, Fish & Chips, or Bacon Cheeseburger. $17.99: 6 oz Rib Eye, Double Hickory Bourbon Chicken, Half Rack of Baby-Back Ribs, or Shrimp Scampi. Each Everyday Fresh Meal comes with unlimited trips to Ruby Tuesday’s signature Garden Bar, featuring more than 60 fresh ingredients, including a variety of dressings, fan-favorite pumpernickel croutons, and chef-prepared salads. Guests can also enjoy a bottomless beverage, with options such as soft drinks, flavored tea, and flavored lemonade. Select entrees are also served with a side, such as fries, a baked potato, mashed potatoes, or a breadstick. For details, visit rubytuesday.com/everyday-fresh-meals. “One of the things that makes Ruby Tuesday special is the variety we offer, from our signature burgers and entrees to our all-you-can-eat Garden Bar,” adds FitzPatrick. “We wanted to bring that variety to the forefront with a selection of meals that gives guests plenty of options, no matter what they’re in the mood for.” This Veterans Day, Ruby Tuesday is thanking the brave men and women who have served or are serving in our U.S. military by inviting U.S. veterans and all active-duty, Reserve, and National Guard service members to enjoy a free Everyday Fresh Meal by showing proof of military service. The offer is valid Wednesday, November 11, 2026, for dine-in only at participating locations. Everyday Fresh Meals are now available at Ruby Tuesday locations nationwide and will also be featured in the brand’s upcoming fall menus, arriving in late November. articles.title: Wonder Takes First Step Toward IPO
articles.titleKo: Wonder Takes First Step Toward IPO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The company's restaurant footprint has grown significantly in recent months, expanding from 46 locations to approximately 140 since its previous funding announcement in May 2025. Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company following years of aggressive expansion and billions of dollars in investment. The food technology company announced Thursday that it confidentially submitted a draft registration statement on Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a proposed initial public offering of Class A common stock. The number of shares Wonder plans to offer and the anticipated price range have not been determined. The potential offering is subject to market conditions, regulatory review, and other factors. The filing marks a significant development for the company founded by entrepreneur Marc Lore, who has assembled a food platform spanning restaurants, delivery, meal kits, and automated kitchen technology. It also follows Wonder’s recent $650 million Series D funding round , which valued the company at $9 billion before the investment. Existing investors Accel, GV, and New Enterprise Associates participated alongside new investments from funds managed by AllianceBernstein, ARK Invest, and Kayne Anderson Rudnick Investment Management. Wonder said the funding would support restaurant expansion, marketplace growth, and continued investments in robotics, AI, and technology. The company’s restaurant footprint has grown significantly in recent months, expanding from 46 locations to approximately 140 since its previous funding announcement in May 2025. Wonder operates a digital food platform that allows customers to order meals from multiple restaurant concepts in a single transaction. Its business includes company-owned restaurants, licensed restaurant brands, local restaurant delivery, and meal solutions. The company has also pursued an aggressive acquisition strategy to expand its capabilities and restaurant portfolio. Its recent purchase of New York City barbecue chain Mighty Quinn’s added eight locations across New York, Florida, and Maryland. Earlier this year, Wonder acquired Blue Ribbon Fried Chicken, which has since expanded across additional Wonder locations. Those deals followed several larger transactions, including the $650 million acquisition of Grubhub, the $186 million purchase of Sweetgreen’s Infinite Kitchen business, and the $103 million acquisition of meal-kit company Blue Apron. The acquisitions have given Wonder access to delivery infrastructure, established restaurant concepts, meal-kit distribution, and automated food preparation technology. Wonder also recently announced a partnership with autonomous drone delivery company Zipline, with plans to introduce on-demand drone delivery in Texas in 2027. Wonder has attracted substantial investment throughout its expansion. Bloomberg reported in 2025 that the company raised $600 million at a valuation exceeding $7 billion. In 2024, Wonder secured another $700 million, including $100 million from Lore. The post Wonder Takes First Step Toward IPO appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Wendy’s is Going Back to Basics to Save its Business
articles.titleKo: Wendy’s is Going Back to Basics to Save its Business
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wendy’s domestic same-restaurant sales declined 5.7 percent in Q3. Wendy’s is giving its U.S. franchisees permission to start the day later. The burger chain will make breakfast optional at every domestic restaurant, a significant shift in its effort to repair restaurant profitability and win back customers. The decision puts the economics of individual locations ahead of a uniform operating schedule as Wendy’s rebuilds a business still losing substantial traffic. The company estimates the change could unlock up to $200 million in restaurant-level EBITDA across franchise and company restaurants. That benefit would come from eliminating breakfast losses and improving margins during the rest of the day. “Mandating that franchisees operate during a daypart where they lose money is going to do nothing but hurt their business,” CEO Bob Wright said during Wendy’s third-quarter earnings call. The breakfast decision is among the most consequential moves under Dave’s Way, Wendy’s multiyear turnaround strategy. The brand chose to move forward with the comeback and rejected a $1.4 billion takeover offer from an investor group led by billionaire Nelson Peltz. Another big move is a proposed acquisition of up to 163 restaurants from bankrupt franchisee Meritage Hospitality Group. READ MORE : New Wendy’s CEO Vows to Restore Quality and Revive Customer Traffic The changes arrive as Wendy’s domestic same-restaurant sales declined 5.7 percent in Q3. Traffic fell 11.9 percent, partially offset by 6.2 percent average check growth. The comparable sales decline improved 130 basis points from Q2, with traffic improving sequentially through each period of the quarter. Global systemwide sales decreased 5.9 percent. Adjusted EBITDA fell $24.6 million to $113.4 million. Wendy’s studied restaurants that had already stopped serving breakfast before extending the option across the country. Those locations improved profitability at lunch, dinner, and late night, and many recovered all their breakfast sales during other dayparts. A shorter operating day allows restaurants to concentrate manager coverage during busier hours. It also reduces waste associated with low-volume periods. The company had discussed the change with franchisees the night before the call and was beginning to provide information to help them evaluate each restaurant. Wendy’s did not disclose how many locations might discontinue breakfast. Restaurants that keep the daypart will continue receiving product, marketing, and operational support. Wright expects a substantial portion of franchisees to identify locations where breakfast fails the profitability test. The same scrutiny of restaurant economics is driving Wendy’s response to Meritage’s bankruptcy. The parties signed a letter of intent earlier in the week under which Wendy’s would acquire up to 163 locations. Those restaurants are concentrated in markets where the company already operates, giving it an existing field organization and local experience to support performance improvements. Other Meritage markets are expected to transition to franchisees through the bankruptcy process. The proposed acquisition also permits higher and better offers from approved franchisees. “This will be, we think, one of the largest, if not the largest acquisition of franchise-to-company restaurants in the company’s history, certainly in a long, long time,” Wright said. Wendy’s could eventually refranchise acquired restaurants, but Wright did not commit to a timetable. The immediate opportunity is to improve operations and participate financially in their recovery. A dedicated portfolio optimization team is working with a small group of franchisees requiring additional support. articles.title: OHG Brands Ready to Tap Into Nostalgia with Leadership Team
articles.titleKo: OHG Brands Ready to Tap Into Nostalgia with Leadership Team
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . While the moniker OHG Brands (standing for Original. Honest. Good) might be new, the concepts under its umbrella are not. That’s a point Anthony Ackil keeps coming back to. Ackil, who created fast casual B.GOOD when he was 26, growing it to 80 stores before selling in 2018, today leads Streetlight Ventures as CEO, an operating and investment company he founded a year after exiting. And now, Ackil and the company sit at the helm of OHG Brands, which emerged in late September as a fresh company from previous FAT Brands. Included are 12 legacy names—Round Table Pizza, Fatburger, Marble Slab Creamery, Johnny Rockets, Fazoli’s, Great American Cookies, Buffalo’s Cafe & Express, Hurricane Grill & Wings, Native Grill & Wings, Pretzelmaker, and Ponderosa and Bonanza Steakhouses—collectively covering 1,700 global units. “I love the brands,” Ackil says in an interview with QSR magazine . “I think they’re iconic. I think there’s strength in them. This idea of a brand being viable for 50 years, like some of our brands—almost all of them—it’s really unique.” The “youngest,” Hurricane Grill & Wings, turned 31 in 2026. When they were founded Round Table Pizza: 1959 Fatburger: 1947 Marble Slab Creamery: 1983 Johnny Rockets: 1986 Fazoli’s: 1988 Great American Cookies: 1977 Buffalo’s Cafe & Express: 1985 (express in 2006) Hurricane Grill & Wings: 1995 Native Grill & Wings: 1978 Pretzelmaker: 1991 Ponderosa: 1965 Bonanza: 1963 (merged in 1989 with Ponderosa) Streetlight Ventures began as a restaurant consulting company with a focus on management, operations, finance, and marketing. When COVID hit, it started taking over brands (it works with concepts like Burton’s Grill & Bar, Anna’s Taqueria, and more ) and was an active buyer. But what it found, like many during pandemic valuation swings, was it couldn’t reach an agreement on price with owners, often founders. Where Streetlight couldn’t acquire the company, though, it started running the business. “And what we created [was] an operating company,” Ackil says. “And it came out of the B.GOOD idea of it’s really hard to run a business. You need every functional area. You need expertise at every different functional area. That’s really where Streetlight came from. It’s the idea of running a business or adding support across every aspect of the business, from finance to marketing to innovation to operations, and lifting the business holistically.” That’s what it’s doing with OHG Brands and its roster of 12 concepts. Streetlight’s team of executives, entrepreneurs, and leaders within the restaurant space, want to drive the business forward by surrounding it with expertise and experience across touchpoints. As part of the effort, OHG announced a host of appointments. Among them: Stephen England, Chief Operating Officer: brings 30-plus years in restaurant operations, including roles as Senior Vice President of Operations at Subway and Vice President of Operating Systems at Dunkin’ Brands. Kelly Hansen, Chief Marketing Officer: brings 20-plus years of restaurant marketing experience spanning QSR to fine dining, including five years in marketing leadership at Raising Cane’s during its period of massive growth. She previously oversaw marketing for Tavistock Restaurant Collection, Lemonade Restaurant Group, and others. Jose Ponce, Chief of Staff and Head of HR: holds more than 15 years of HR experience spanning organizational design, talent strategy, and building HR departments from the ground up across high-growth restaurant and franchise businesses, including Burger King, Tim Hortons, and Popeyes. Artie Jones, General Counsel: formerly Associate General Counsel and VP at BJ’s Wholesale Club, where he advised on complex commercial transactions, enterprise risk, corporate governance, regulatory compliance, employment and litigation strategy, and helped modernize the legal department. articles.title: Coca-Cola Femsa investe R$ 75 milhões em centro de distribuição em Limeira
articles.titleKo: Coca-Cola Femsa investe R$ 75 milhões em centro de distribuição em Limeira
articles.originalSummary: A Coca-Cola Femsa Brasil vai inaugurar um novo centro de distribuição em Limeira, no interior de São Paulo, com investimento estimado em R$ 75 milhões. Desenvolvida no modelo build-to-suit (BTS), a estrutura tem início das atividades previsto para outubro de 2027 e ampliará a capacidade logística da companhia na região. “A nova operação em Limeira representa um importante investimento da Coca-Cola Femsa Brasil, que contribuirá para a geração inicial de 400 oportunidades de emprego e para o desenvolvimento econômico da região. Ao mesmo tempo, fortalecerá nossa estrutura logística, permitindo atender mais de 7,5 mil clientes com mais agilidade e eficiência e nos aproximar ainda mais dos consumidores”, afirma Eduardo Pereyra, CEO da Coca-Cola Femsa Brasil. O centro contará com 4.848 posições de armazenamento e terá capacidade para distribuir todo o portfólio da Coca-Cola Femsa Brasil. A operação atenderá 22 municípios do interior paulista. O empreendimento será instalado às margens da Rodovia Deputado Laércio Corte, conhecida como Limeira-Piracicaba, com acesso às rodovias dos Bandeirantes e Washington Luís. “Limeira tem localização estratégica, infraestrutura e condições favoráveis para receber grandes empreendimentos. A Prefeitura trabalha para apresentar essas vantagens ao mercado e criar oportunidades para a chegada de novos investimentos. A instalação de um dos maiores centros de distribuição da Coca-Cola Femsa no estado reforça esse potencial e representa mais empregos e desenvolvimento para a cidade”, diz o prefeito Murilo Félix. Crescimento de 3,9% em volume no Brasil A Coca-Cola Femsa reportou ao mercado crescimento de 3,9% no volume de bebidas comercializadas no Brasil no terceiro trimestre de 2026 , na comparação com o mesmo período do ano passado. O resultado contribuiu para o avanço das operações da companhia na América do Sul, mas não afastou as preocupações do BTG Pactual com o desempenho do mercado brasileiro em 2027. Em relatório divulgado nesta quarta-feira, 28, o banco projeta estabilidade dos volumes vendidos no País no próximo ano, em um cenário de custo elevado de capital e menor previsibilidade para o consumo. A avaliação acompanha a divulgação dos resultados trimestrais da Coca-Cola Femsa, maior engarrafadora de produtos Coca-Cola do mundo em volume de vendas. Globalmente, a companhia registrou receita de 79,72 bilhões de pesos mexicanos, crescimento de 10,9% em relação ao terceiro trimestre de 2025. Desconsiderando os efeitos cambiais, o avanço foi de 11,3%. articles.title: Privalia passa a oferecer entrega no próximo dia útil em São Paulo
articles.titleKo: Privalia passa a oferecer entrega no próximo dia útil em São Paulo
articles.originalSummary: A Privalia passa a oferecer entrega no próximo dia útil para compras realizadas até o meio-dia, de segunda a sexta-feira. A modalidade, sem cobrança adicional, já está disponível na capital paulista e em sete municípios da Grande São Paulo. A iniciativa amplia os serviços logísticos da plataforma digital de moda e lifestyle, que reúne 20 milhões de clientes no Brasil. O serviço já alcança mais de 98% dos pedidos de produtos participantes na cidade de São Paulo, além de Barueri, Osasco, Guarulhos, Santo André, São Bernardo do Campo, São Caetano do Sul e Mauá. A empresa prevê levar a modalidade a pelo menos outras 20 cidades da Grande São Paulo até o fim de novembro. “A Privalia é conhecida pelas oportunidades de comprar grandes marcas a preços atrativos, e isso não muda. O que faltava era estarmos presentes também quando o cliente precisa do produto para amanhã. Com a entrega no próximo dia útil, passamos a atender essas duas necessidades na mesma plataforma”, afirma Cesar Borges, COO da Privalia. Ainda em 2026, a Privalia pretende expandir a entrega no próximo dia útil para outras regiões, incluindo Belo Horizonte, Campinas e Curitiba. A política de frete da plataforma, incluindo as condições de gratuidade quando aplicáveis, permanece inalterada. As campanhas participantes estão identificadas no site e no aplicativo com o selo “entrega rápida”, permitindo que o consumidor identifique os produtos elegíveis antes de finalizar a compra. Entre as marcas participantes estão Live!, Insider, Lança Perfume e Hering. Operação logística Para viabilizar o novo prazo, a Privalia ajustou os processos de preparação e despacho dos pedidos, alinhando estoque, centro de distribuição e transportadoras. Antes do lançamento, a modalidade passou por uma fase piloto que envolveu cerca de 30 mil entregas. Durante as campanhas de 11.11 e Black Friday, a proposta é manter a entrega no próximo dia útil para todos os produtos identificados como entrega rápida nas regiões atendidas. A modalidade está disponível desde a primeira semana de novembro, no site e no aplicativo da Privalia. articles.title: Presidente do Paraguai renuncia em meio à crise bancária; vice assume
articles.titleKo: Presidente do Paraguai renuncia em meio à crise bancária; vice assume
articles.originalSummary: Enquanto a Câmara dos Deputados do Paraguai discutia a abertura de um processo de impeachment contra o presidente, nesta quinta-feira, 5, o mandatário do país Santiago Peña anunciou a renúncia ao cargo, em meio a uma crise financeira causada pela intervenção do Banco Central Paraguaio (BCP) no banco digital Ueno Bank. Abandonado pelo próprio partido, que passou a cobrar sua renúncia, Peña justificou a decisão em nome da estabilidade do país e da necessidade de “preservar nossas instituições”. O vice-presidente Pedro Allana assumirá o cargo. “Me dirijo a vocês em um dos momentos mais difíceis da minha vida, com o coração voltado para o Paraguai e com a convicção de que a nossa República deve estar sempre acima de qualquer pessoa ou circunstância”, disse o presidente, em pronunciamento nas redes sociais. “A história se encarregará de julgar e colocar na sua devida dimensão os acontecimentos que hoje nos cabe vivenciar. Tomei a decisão de apresentar a minha renúncia à Presidência da República”, acrescentou. Crise A crise financeira que sacudiu o Paraguai começou na terça-feira, 3, e se transformou em crise política. Na manhã de hoje, a Câmara iniciou o debate para abertura de um processo de impeachment que contava com o apoio até mesmo da legenda do mandatário, o Partido Colorado. O terremoto político no país vizinho é consequência da liquidação do Ueno Bank, que tinha 2,9 milhões de correntistas, cerca de 60% da população adulta do país. Essas pessoas tiveram seus depósitos congelados. Após a liquidação do banco, o presidente do BC paraguaio, Carlos Carvallo, renunciou ao cargo. Ele foi dirigente do banco digital até 2023, antes de assumir a chefia do Banco Central do país. https Protestos de rua cobram que os responsáveis pela crise sejam punidos. O Ministério Público do Paraguai pediu a prisão de oito pessoas, incluindo o presidente do Ueno, Juan Manuel Gustale. Presidência A crise atingiu o presidente Santiago Peña por ele ter sido acionista, até março de 2025, do grupo que controla o banco, o Grupo Vázquez. Eleito em 2023, o Santiago Peña é um político da direita conservadora do Partido Colorado que há sete décadas controla o poder no Paraguai, exceto por cinco anos (1947-1952). A oposição acusa o governo pelos investimentos realizados pelo Instituto de Seguridade Social (PIS), que é estatal, no Ueno Bank. O banco digital ainda administra o pagamento de pensões de milhares de aposentados e tem cerca de 30% dos depósitos de fundos públicos, estimados em US$ 850 milhões. A oposição responsabiliza Peña pela crise por ele ter nomeado para presidente do BC um ex-dirigente do Ueno. Ao anunciar a renúncia, o presidente pediu desculpas ao povo paraguaio. “Também quero pedir desculpas ao povo, caso em algum momento eu tenha falhado. Nunca foi minha intenção trair a confiança que depositaram em mim. A cada dia, assumi esta responsabilidade com a vontade de trabalhar pelo Paraguai”, afirmou Peña. Partido Colorado O presidente do Partido Colorado e ex-presidente do país, Horácio Cartes, afirmou que a legenda não estará ao lado “do latrocínio de fundos públicos, privados e dos aposentados”. O presidente do Congresso paraguaio, Bachi Nunéz, dois dias antes de pedir a renúncia de Peña, avaliava à imprensa que o presidente não poderia ser responsabilizado porque o Banco Central tinha autonomia institucional. A oposição acusa o Partido Colorado de querer se afastar do escândalo que teria ajudado a construir. A deputada do Partido País Solidário (PPS), Johanna Ortega, destacou, durante a sessão da Câmara, que os recursos dos aposentados estavam sendo depositados em um banco próximo ao presidente Peña. “Temos alertado sobre conflitos de interesses, sobre a utilização de instituições públicas para favorecer negócios privados de uns poucos, e sobre o crime de gestão em proveito próprio — prática na qual este Presidente da República tem incorrido sistematicamente”, afirmou. O Paraguai conta com um fundo garantidor que pode reembolsar até US$ 38 m

articles.title: CEO da Cimed é alvo de queixa-crime por suposto uso de fórmulas da Suavetex
articles.titleKo: CEO da Cimed é alvo de queixa-crime por suposto uso de fórmulas da Suavetex
articles.originalSummary: A fabricante de produtos de higiene pessoal Suavetex apresentou queixa-crime contra João Adibe, CEO da Cimed, por suposto uso indevido de informações técnicas obtidas durante negociações societárias. Segundo o site Metrópoles , a empresa acusa o executivo de utilizar formulações desenvolvidas por ela no lançamento de seis produtos de higiene bucal. De acordo com a publicação, a Suavetex afirma que as formulações foram compartilhadas com a Cimed para viabilizar o registro dos produtos na Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa). A proposta de sociedade previa que a Suavetex seria responsável pela fabricação, enquanto a Cimed cuidaria da distribuição dos produtos por meio da marca Carmed 12 horas. Em resposta à reportagem da Mercado&Consumo , a Cimed afirma que a queixa-crime representa mais uma tentativa da Suavetex de reverter as sucessivas derrotas que vem sofrendo na esfera cível. “A Cimed confia que o Poder Judiciário, como já fez, reconhecerá a improcedência das alegações.” “Esse posicionamento tem sido reconhecido de forma consistente pelo Poder Judiciário, tanto em decisões de primeira quanto de segunda instância, que vêm reiteradamente negando os pedidos apresentados pela Suavetex”, diz a empresa. A Cimed também considera “especialmente grave a tentativa da Suavetex de transformar uma controvérsia comercial, marcada pelo insucesso das medidas adotadas na esfera cível, em uma verdadeira aventura jurídica de natureza criminal”. “A companhia não admitirá imputações falsas ou infundadas que atinjam a honra e a reputação de seus representantes. Acusações dessa natureza terão consequências jurídicas, e a Cimed adotará todas as medidas cabíveis, nas esferas cível e criminal, para responsabilizar seus autores”, completa. articles.title: Highland Brewing Celebrates 30 Years of Cold Mountain with a Weekend of Festivities
articles.titleKo: Highland Brewing Celebrates 30 Years of Cold Mountain with a Weekend of Festivities
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Milestone celebration features beer dinner with James Beard-winning chef Taylor Montgomery, rare anniversary beers, live music and five days of Cold Mountain. Highland Brewing’s Cold Mountain is not just a seasonal winter ale—it’s an Asheville holiday tradition that attracts thousands of beer lovers each year. November 12-16, Asheville’s original craft brewery celebrates 30 years of Cold Mountain Winter Ale with new and limited anniversary beers, a culinary collaboration with one of the South’s most celebrated chefs, the opening of Oscar’s Pizza, and five days of music and festivities. Cold Mountain Winter Ale is a 5.9% ABV spiced winter ale, with notes of vanilla, hazelnut, dark fruit and cinnamon. More than just a beer, its release has become a yearly tradition that marks the unofficial start of the holiday season in Western North Carolina. “Cold Mountain’s 30-year history is incredible to consider,” said Leah Wong Ashburn, President and CEO of Highland Brewing. “The release weekend brings people back to Highland year after year to mark the start of the holiday season and the beer brings them home to be with family and friends. Dad started this brewery with a commitment to great beer and community, so the way Highland fans celebrate and share Cold Mountain is special. Credit for the magic belongs to our inspiring Highland team. Cold Mountain the beer and Cold Mountain the weekend deliver on tradition and new experiences every year.” This year, Cold Mountain Winter Ale returns in bottles and on draft, with the original and three spin-offs featured in a special 30th Anniversary Variety Pack of 16-ounce cans: Cold Mountain Winter Ale, returning Coconut Cold Mountain, and two new releases: Chocolate Orange Cold Mountain, which pairs rich chocolate with bright citrus notes; and Pumpkin Spice Latte Cold Mountain, featuring notes of cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves and coffee. The three spin-offs are also available in four-packs of 16-ounce cans. The commemorative packaging features an original illustrated design inspired by Nova, a gray wolf at Asheville’s WNC Nature Center, one of Highland’s Thirst for Good community partners, along with special 30th anniversary bottle crowns. Taproom-only versions of Cold Mountain Winter Ale on draft include Chai, Sour Cherry, Apple Cider Donut and Imperial Cold Mountain. Two limited barrel-aged releases will also be available on draft and in 500 mL bottles: Barrel-Aged Cold Mountain (11% ABV) and the first-ever bottled Double Barrel-Aged Bourbon Pecan Cold Mountain (13% ABV). Guests attending Friday and Saturday also have the chance to sample a super-limited Triple Barrel-Aged Cold Mountain, non-carbonated and tapped directly from the barrel. Don’t miss your chance to enjoy Cold Mountain Winter Ale among friends during Highland Brewing’s annual Cold Mountain event! Here’s what to expect: Thursday, Nov. 12: 7th Annual Cold Mountain Beer Dinner (SOLD OUT): The festivities begin with Highland’s 7th Annual Cold Mountain Beer Dinner from 5-9 p.m. on Nov. 12! Chef Taylor Montgomery of Montgomery Sky Farm , the 2026 James Beard Award winner for Best Chef: Southeast, will curate a multi-course dinner paired with Cold Mountain releases and specialty offerings. Friday, Nov. 13: Live Music: Grab your favorite 2026 version of Cold Mountain Winter Ale and join Highland Brewing for a full day of live music from noon to 11 p.m. Groove to the funky-but-chic sounds of Pleasure Chest , dance along with high-energy Ska City , stomp your boots to the twangy, genre-bending country music of Heavenly Vipers and experience the psychedelic adventure-rock and jam-fusion sounds of New Dawn Starkestra . Beyond the live music, Friday’s festivities include a Cold Mountain Heritage Panel featuring Leah Ashburn, Nikki Mitchell, Jamie Rowe and Joshua Jiles celebrating three decades of the iconic winter ale,

articles.title: Fenabrave prevê aumento de 12,8% na venda de veículos novos em 2026
articles.titleKo: Fenabrave prevê aumento de 12,8% na venda de veículos novos em 2026
articles.originalSummary: A Federação Nacional da Distribuição de Veículos Automotores (Fenabrave) aumentou a projeção de crescimento para as vendas de veículos novos em 2026 de 8,6% para 12,8%. A expectativa foi divulgada nesta quarta-feira, 4, com os dados de emplacamentos de veículos novos no País em outubro. A previsão é de que o setor, como um todo, deve vender quase 5,6 milhões de unidades no ano. Entre janeiro e outubro, foram emplacadas 4.722.650 unidades, o que já representa um crescimento de 12,62% sobre igual período de 2025. De acordo com a Fenabrave, este foi o segundo maior resultado acumulado da série histórica, atrás apenas do registrado em 2011. “Os resultados acumulados permitem uma avaliação mais favorável para o fechamento do ano, principalmente entre automóveis e comerciais leves. Ao mesmo tempo, continuamos projetando retração para caminhões e ônibus, ainda que menores que as estimadas em julho, mas abaixo do que prevíamos em janeiro”, disse Arcelio Junior, presidente da Fenabrave. Para a federação, o resultado mostra que o mercado brasileiro mantém ritmo consistente de crescimento, ainda que com ajustes pontuais. “Observamos uma recuperação gradual em segmentos como caminhões, ônibus e implementos rodoviários, cuja queda acentuada vem retrocedendo ao longo dos meses, notadamente, após a implantação do Programa Move Brasil”, acrescentou Arcelio Junior. Queda em outubro As vendas desses veículos tiveram queda de 4,06% em outubro, na comparação com setembro, segundo o balanço. Em relação a outubro de 2025, também houve retração, de 0,85%. A Fenabrave avalia que a retração de outubro foi influenciada pelo calendário, já que outubro do ano passado teve 23 dias úteis, enquanto neste ano foram 21. O total de 489.119 emplacamentos no mês passado inclui automóveis, veículos comerciais leves (picapes e furgões), ônibus, caminhões, motos e implementos rodoviários, como reboques e carrocerias. Veículos elétricos Um fator que tem contribuído para o bom desempenho no ano é a venda dos veículos eletrificados, que apresentaram crescimento superior a 130% no acumulado do ano, com 524.766 unidades emplacadas. Isso considera tanto os modelos híbridos quanto os totalmente elétricos. Considerando-se apenas automóveis e veículos comerciais leves, a participação dos eletrificados praticamente dobrou no país: atualmente, eles já representam 20,54% dos emplacamentos no Brasil, diz a Fenabrave. No ano passado, isso correspondia a 10,67%. Desempenho por segmentos O segmento de automóveis e comerciais leves continua tendo um bom crescimento no ano, informou a Fenabrave. No acumulado do ano, o crescimento foi de 17,29%, com 2.410.505 unidades emplacadas. Considerando-se apenas o mês de outubro, houve queda de 5,48% em relação a setembro e crescimento de 2,5% ante outubro do ano passado. Quanto aos segmentos de caminhões e ônibus, a queda persiste, apesar de alguma recuperação no ano. No acumulado do ano, o recuo foi de 4,18%, enquanto, em setembro, a queda foi de 8,36%. Em relação a outubro de 2025, as vendas caíram 10,26%. Já as motocicletas cresceram 8,90% no ano, com 1.985.816 unidades emplacadas, maior volume acumulado de sua série histórica. “A motocicleta atende tanto às necessidades de mobilidade individual quanto às atividades profissionais, especialmente nas cidades. Essa diversidade de utilização contribui para manter a demanda elevada, ainda que com pequenos ajustes pontuais de um mês para o outro, como os que ocorreram em outubro, em função do menor número de dias úteis em relação a outubro do ano passado”, afirma Arcelio Junior. Seasonal innovation performed better with the brand’s core audience, while an $11.99 bowl promo was bringing in younger guests. “We had just always assumed that younger guests wanted new flavors and seasonal trends,” said Moré. “Now we know price point is the lever that’s actually driving younger customers versus the LTOs we were running.” Bikky AI turns Sonny’s data into action, working directly from the brand’s own sales, menu, and guest data to dig into complex questions without manual reporting. “I am in the chat all day long. I use Bikky as my source of truth and it’s a good pulse check against our internal reporting.” said Moré. Katelyn uses Bikky AI for location-level analysis and year-over-year holiday comparisons that previously took hours. “Being able to look at Labor Day over Labor Day last year through Bikky is so seamless,” said Moré. “Prior to Bikky, I’d have to pull four sets of data to compare that.” Sonny’s is also catching menu wins earlier. articles.title: Construção defende período de transição de 5 anos para acabar com jornada 6×1
articles.titleKo: Construção defende período de transição de 5 anos para acabar com jornada 6×1
articles.originalSummary: A Câmara Brasileira da Indústria da Construção (CBIC) entregou ao Ministério do Trabalho um documento composto por 11 pleitos para amenizar os efeitos da mudança na jornada de trabalho com o fim da escala 6×1. Segundo a CBIC, a principal reivindicação é a ampliação do período de transição para cinco anos, permitindo que as empresas reorganizem suas operações, renegociem contratos e invistam em qualificação profissional e inovação tecnológica. Outro ponto é a definição de um divisor nacional para o cálculo do valor da hora trabalhada. A CBIC propõe a adoção de divisores de 255 horas para jornadas de 42 horas semanais e de 243 horas para jornadas de 40 horas, ambas na escala 5×2. Segundo a entidade empresarial, a medida busca estabelecer critérios uniformes e evitar interpretações divergentes que possam gerar insegurança jurídica e aumento dos encargos trabalhistas. A entidade também propõe que a regulamentação reconheça expressamente a possibilidade de distribuir a jornada de 42 horas semanais em cinco dias, com carga diária de 8 horas e 24 minutos, sem que os 24 minutos excedentes à oitava hora sejam considerados horas extras. O pleito prevê ainda que a adequação da jornada possa ser estabelecida por meio de acordos ou convenções coletivas, garantindo maior segurança jurídica a ambas as partes. Entre as reivindicações está ainda a criação de regras específicas de compensação de jornada para a construção civil, considerando as particularidades dos canteiros, sujeitos a condições climáticas, paralisações técnicas e diferentes etapas de execução. A CBIC defende mecanismos negociáveis de compensação semanal e mensal, além de sistemas de banco de horas compatíveis com a dinâmica do setor. O documento também propõe critérios claros para o descanso semanal remunerado, a fim de garantir previsibilidade na organização das equipes. Em relação aos feriados, a entidade pede que a coincidência com dias de descanso não gere automaticamente folgas adicionais, créditos em banco de horas ou pagamentos em dobro. A entidade também defende a criação de parâmetros nacionais uniformes para a regulamentação, evitando que questões como divisores salariais, compensações e descanso semanal sejam submetidas a interpretações distintas em cada região do País. Por fim, a CBIC propõe ajustes nas regras de transição do Bolsa Família , permitindo que beneficiários ingressem ou retornem ao mercado formal sem perda imediata do auxílio. A medida busca ampliar a oferta de trabalhadores e estimular a formalização, preservando a proteção social durante esse processo. Na quarta-feira, 4, uma comitiva da CBIC liderada pelo presidente Eduardo Aroeira Almeida se reuniu em Brasília com o ministro do Trabalho e Emprego, Luiz Marinho. A principal preocupação da CBIC está relacionada à dificuldade de adaptação de um setor intensivo em mão de obra, que já enfrenta escassez de trabalhadores. Pelas contagens da entidade, a redução da jornada poderá representar a perda de quase 600 milhões de horas de trabalho por ano, exigindo a contratação de aproximadamente 300 mil novos profissionais para manter a atual capacidade produtiva. Segundo a associação empresarial, a elevação prevista dos custos de mão de obra gira entre 10% e 15%. A construção civil tem, hoje, um recorde de pessoas empregadas no setor, com 3,150 milhões de trabalhadores com carteira assinada no País, aumento de 3% em relação a igual mês de 2025. O número é o mais alto desde o início da pesquisa do novo Cadastro Geral de Empregados e Desempregados (Caged), iniciada em janeiro de 2020, conforme dados compilados pela CBIC. Nos primeiros oito meses de 2026, a construção criou 200,4 mil novos empregos. Com o mercado de trabalho aquecido na construção, o salário médio para quem está ingressando no setor é de R$ 2.642,46, mantendo-se acima da média nacional dos salários de entrada, que é de R$ 2.410,74. articles.title: Havan inaugura megaloja de número 200 com fachada comemorativa em Roraima
articles.titleKo: Havan inaugura megaloja de número 200 com fachada comemorativa em Roraima
articles.originalSummary: A Havan prepara uma fachada especial para celebrar a inauguração de sua megaloja de número 200, marcada para sábado, 14 de novembro, em Boa Vista (RR). A unidade terá uma logomarca comemorativa e marcará um novo capítulo na expansão da varejista, que completa 40 anos em 2026. A escolha de Boa Vista representa também a chegada da empresa a mais um Estado brasileiro. Roraima ainda não contava com uma megaloja da Havan, que se aproxima do objetivo de estar presente em todo o País. O Ceará será o próximo destino, com uma unidade prevista para Fortaleza a partir de 12 de dezembro. “Chegar à megaloja de número 200 justamente no ano em que completamos 40 anos é a realização de um sonho construído com muito trabalho, coragem e dedicação. Queremos que essa conquista fique marcada na memória dos brasileiros e que todos se lembrem de que, juntos, alcançamos uma meta histórica. Inaugurar essa loja em Boa Vista, levando a Havan a mais um Estado, torna tudo ainda mais especial”, afirma o dono da Havan, Luciano Hang . A nova loja será a mais distante da matriz da Havan, em Brusque (SC), e do Centro de Distribuição Havan (CDH), em Barra Velha (SC). A operação logística para transportar a Estátua da Liberdade, símbolo da varejista, percorreu cerca de seis mil quilômetros entre Camboriú (SC) e Boa Vista. O transporte levou 15 dias pelas rodovias e outros oito dias de balsa, tornando-se a maior operação logística já realizada pela Havan para transportar uma Estátua da Liberdade. articles.title: Oxxo aposta em mídia exterior com tecnologia 3D e integração à paisagem urbana
articles.titleKo: Oxxo aposta em mídia exterior com tecnologia 3D e integração à paisagem urbana
articles.originalSummary: A rede de lojas de proximidade Oxxo apostou em uma ação de mídia exterior que combina tecnologia e criatividade para ampliar a visibilidade de suas ofertas em Santos, no litoral de São Paulo. Desenvolvido pela Chicooh+, OOH Tech especializada em mídia exterior, em parceria com a Agência Mestiça, o projeto reúne diferentes formatos de OOH e DOOH, com destaque para uma banca digital que exibe conteúdo 3D anamórfico. Com exibição realizada pela I Mídia Painéis Publicitários Ltda. ME, a iniciativa explora novas possibilidades de comunicação na paisagem urbana e incorpora o conceito de mídia regenerativa, que propõe uma atuação da publicidade exterior para além da veiculação de mensagens comerciais. “A mídia exterior faz parte da paisagem das cidades e tem potencial para construir relações mais interessantes com os espaços e as pessoas que circulam por eles. A banca é um exemplo de como podemos pensar a comunicação para além da mensagem publicitária, considerando também a presença visual do ativo e sua relação com o entorno”, afirma Chico Preto, CEO da Chicooh+. Instalada em meio à vegetação, a banca digital chama a atenção para a presença da publicidade no cotidiano da cidade. A proposta também busca explorar como o mobiliário urbano pode contribuir para uma experiência visual que vá além da exposição de ofertas. A estratégia inclui bancas, painéis digitais e totens em formatos estáticos e digitais, distribuindo a comunicação por diferentes pontos de circulação de Santos. Parte do conteúdo exibido na banca foi produzida pela Bridge Content e utiliza o recurso 3D anamórfico para criar uma sensação de profundidade e ampliar o impacto visual da peça. A tecnologia permite explorar as características da tela e transformar o próprio suporte em parte da ideia criativa. Dessa forma, a comunicação do Oxxo combina recursos digitais e presença física no ambiente urbano para chamar a atenção de quem circula pelo entorno. articles.title: Receita apreende 15 toneladas de produtos irregulares no Porto do Rio
articles.titleKo: Receita apreende 15 toneladas de produtos irregulares no Porto do Rio
articles.originalSummary: A Receita Federal apreendeu, nesta quarta-feira, 4, contêiner com aproximadamente 15 toneladas de mercadorias irregulares no Porto do Rio de Janeiro. A carga, proveniente da China, continha cerca de 243 mil itens e foi avaliada em R$ 3,6 milhões. Durante a fiscalização, a mercadoria foi inicialmente declarada como guarda-chuvas, produtos de baixo valor comercial. No entanto, a verificação física realizada pelos servidores da Receita Federal revelou a presença de cosméticos importados sem a devida anuência da Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa), além de produtos com indícios de fraude de marcas regularmente registradas no Brasil. A apreensão integra as ações da Operação Fronteira Receita Federal 2026, iniciativa de vigilância e repressão em rotas utilizadas para a prática de ilícitos como contrabando, descaminho e tráfico de drogas, armas, fauna e flora. A ação reúne órgãos de segurança pública, fiscalização e defesa, promovendo o compartilhamento de inteligência e a atuação integrada no combate ao crime organizado. Ao impedir a entrada de produtos irregulares no mercado nacional, a Receita Federal contribui para a proteção da saúde e da segurança dos consumidores, para a defesa da propriedade intelectual e para a promoção de um ambiente de concorrência leal entre as empresas que atuam regularmente no País. Anvisa interdita terminal no Porto de Santos Nesta terça-feira, 3, a Anvisa determinou a interdição parcial do Brasil Terminal Portuário (BTP), no Porto de Santos, em São Paulo. A decisão foi tomada após uma fiscalização de rotina identificar irregularidades sanitárias durante uma análise de risco. A resolução da Gerência-Geral de Portos, Aeroportos, Fronteiras e Recintos Alfandegados da agência está publicada no Diário Oficial da União. A fiscalização constatou a ausência de área reservada ao armazenamento de produtos com suspeita de comprometimento da qualidade ou interditados pelas autoridades sanitárias. O espaço, de acordo com a regulamentação, deve atender a requisitos específicos de conservação e controle de temperatura. A inspeção também identificou a falta de áreas separadas, trancadas e de acesso restrito para a guarda de substâncias e medicamentos sujeitos a controle especial, em diferentes condições de temperatura, como exige a legislação sanitária. Com informações de Agência Brasil. Imagem: Tânia Rêgo/Agência Brasil O post Receita apreende 15 toneladas de produtos irregulares no Porto do Rio apareceu primeiro em Mercado&Consumo .

articles.title: Someburros Celebrates 40 Years with Anniversary Fiesta in Scottsdale
articles.titleKo: Someburros Celebrates 40 Years with Anniversary Fiesta in Scottsdale
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Someburros, the locally owned and family-operated Mexican restaurant group that has been serving Arizona since 1986, is celebrating 40 years of family, flavor and tradition with its 40th Anniversary Fiesta on Saturday, November 14, 2026, from 3 to 9 p.m. at Salt River Fields at Talking Stick in Scottsdale. The Fiesta celebrates four decades of bringing people together over homemade Sonoran-style Mexican food and honors the guests, employees, partners and communities who made Someburros a local favorite. With tickets starting at $10, guests can enjoy live music, food and family-friendly activities, and Someburros hopes to welcome thousands of Arizonans. “Reaching 40 years is an incredible milestone for our family, and we wouldn’t be here without the support of the Arizona community,” said Tim Vasquez, Owner and President of Someburros. “What started with our family’s recipes and a passion for bringing people together has grown into something much bigger than a restaurant. This Fiesta is our way of saying thank you to the guests who have supported us, the team members who bring our traditions to life every day, and the communities that have welcomed us into their neighborhoods. We look forward to celebrating this special milestone with everyone.” A Fiesta Four Decades in the Making The Someburros 40th Anniversary Fiesta will feature a variety of entertainment and activities for guests of all ages, including: Live Entertainment: Enjoy performances by Rock Lobster and Selena The Show, along with DJs and performances from local communities. Food and Festive Flavors: Guests can purchase Someburros favorites and enjoy a variety of food options throughout the event. Someburros Cantina: Celebrate with refreshing beverages and festive drinks in a lively gathering space. Games and Raffles: Participate in games, raffles and opportunities to win prizes like a trip to Disneyland, Arizona Cardinals memorabilia, and much more. Kid Zone: A dedicated area featuring activities and entertainment for younger guests. Story Village: Explore 40 years of Someburros history, family recipes and the memories that have helped shape the Arizona-born brand. Spectacular Drone Show: End the evening with a dazzling drone show lighting up the Arizona sky, creating a memorable finale to Someburros’ 40th Anniversary Fiesta and celebrating four decades of family, flavor and community. The evening will also include a special Someburros presentation and thank-you celebration, recognizing the people and communities behind the company’s four decades of success. Tickets General admission tickets are $10, VIP tickets are $30, and children ages 5 and under receive free admission. VIP tickets include a bean and cheese mini burro, an exclusive tequila tasting, double raffle tickets and access to a private section with seating near the stage. Parking is free for ticketed guests. Supporting Rancho Feliz Proceeds from the Fiesta benefit Rancho Feliz, a nonprofit serving families in Agua Prieta, Mexico, through education, housing, social services and community programs. The partnership reflects Someburros’ commitment to giving back and making this milestone celebration meaningful beyond the event itself. Forty Years of Family, Flavor and Tradition Founded in Tempe in 1986, Someburros grew from the cherished recipes of family matriarch Nana Isabel Vasquez. Today, the company operates 19 locations across the Phoenix area and Flagstaff, and the Fiesta is a chance to both celebrate that legacy and welcome new guests into the Someburros familia. Tickets and event information are available at www.someburros.com/40thanniversary. The post Someburros Celebrates 40 Years with Anniversary Fiesta in Scottsdale appeared first on QSR Magazine .

Nemco Food Equipment, a third-generation, family-owned manufacturer of commercial foodservice equipment, announces the promotion of Cory Shank from Vice President of Finance to Chief Operating Officer (COO). articles.title: Prince St. Pizza Teams Up with ‘NCIS: New York’ for Veterans Day Fundraiser
articles.titleKo: Prince St. Pizza Teams Up with ‘NCIS: New York’ for Veterans Day Fundraiser
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Prince St. Pizza, the New York City-born pizzeria known for its Sicilian-style square pies and signature pepperoni-loaded slices, is serving up a little extra appreciation this Veterans Day. On Nov. 11, the brand will donate 10% of in-store sales at participating locations to the American Red Cross Service to the Armed Forces program. Through a partnership with CBS’ “NCIS: NEW YORK”, the donation will be matched up to $10,000. Service to the Armed Forces provides critical support services to military members and their families, connecting loved ones during deployments and emergencies and providing care and comfort at military and veteran hospitals. Prince St. Pizza is also thanking those who served with a FREE slice of pizza at all of its locations on Veterans Day. Veterans and active-duty military can claim a slice at the counter by showing a valid military ID or proof of service.* “Prince St. Pizza has always been about bringing people together, and we’re glad to put that spirit behind a cause that matters so much,” said Lawrence Longo, CEO of Prince St. Pizza. “With the support of our guests and ‘NCIS: NEW YORK’, we can help the Red Cross continue supporting service members and their families every day, not just on Veterans Day.” Prince St. has made a habit of celebrity team-ups, and this one arrives as the recently launched drama continues to draw viewers. Cast members Devin Druid, Shane Harper and Jacqueline Byers will be at the Brooklyn location on Nov. 11, handing out slices to fans and veterans. “NCIS: NEW YORK has the privilege of telling stories about people who serve, and now on Veterans Day our focus is to honor the real men and women who have served our country and the families who have supported them,” said Byron Balasco, executive producer and showrunner of NCIS: NEW YORK. “We’re proud to join Prince St. Pizza and the American Red Cross in saying thank you and showing our appreciation.” “I’m so grateful that NCIS: NEW YORK and Prince St. Pizza are joining forces to honor and celebrate military service members and veterans this Veterans Day”, said Joshua Cain, Division Director of the American Red Cross Service to the Armed Forces. “As a veteran myself, I am inspired by their support and collaboration.” Founded in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood over a decade ago, Prince St. Pizza has become a national destination for its crave-worthy square pies, now served at over 20 locations across the U.S. and Canada. For more information, visit princestreetpizza.com . *Offer available for any slice. One slice per person. Must show valid proof of service. articles.title: Crisp & Green Opens in Chaska, Minnesota
articles.titleKo: Crisp & Green Opens in Chaska, Minnesota
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . CRISP & GREEN, a fast-casual dining destination known for its convenient, chef-crafted and health-focused menu, today announced it is continuing its strong momentum in Minnesota with the opening of a new restaurant in Chaska. The location marks the brand’s 23rd in Minnesota, where the brand got its start almost 10 years ago. The Chaska opening reinforces CRISP & GREEN’s response to increasing demand for convenient, better-for-you dining and the brand’s continued momentum as it grows nationwide. “Minnesota is where CRISP & GREEN started, and nearly a decade later, it continues to be one of our greatest opportunities for growth,” said Steele Smiley, Founder and Executive Chairman of CRISP & GREEN. “As we quickly approach the milestone of 100 restaurants nationwide, opening our 23rd location in our home state is especially meaningful. It’s a reflection of how far we’ve come, the strength of the communities that have supported us, and the tremendous opportunity we see ahead as we continue building CRISP & GREEN into a nationally recognized brand.” CRISP & GREEN’s Chaska location is operated by franchise partner M3 Holdings, a seasoned multi-brand operator with expertise in the restaurant and wellness sectors, including ownership of multiple Planet Fitness locations. Since joining CRISP & GREEN in 2023, M3 Holdings has expanded the brand throughout Minnesota, Iowa and Ohio. By the end of 2026, M3 will own 9 locations with several in the pipeline opening as soon as Q1 in 2027. This growth helps to accelerate CRISP & GREEN’s broader system momentum, reinforcing how corporate and franchise development works hand-in-hand to bring the brand’s vision to life nationwide. “Continuing to invest in Twin Cities communities is a priority for our group, and Chaska felt like a natural next step in our growth,” said Alex Mortensen, President of M3 Holdings. “We believe making healthy food more accessible makes healthy choices easier. Our vision is for CRISP & GREEN to become a convenient part of people’s everyday lives, whether they’re commuting to work, taking their kids to practice, or simply looking for a fresh, nutritious meal on the go.” CRISP & GREEN expansion activities are underpinned by a unique model that balances corporate-owned restaurants with a growing roster of franchise partners, ensuring consistency in execution while scaling quickly to meet demand. Since its founding in 2016, CRISP & GREEN has carved out a distinctive niche in the healthy fast-casual space, blending chef-crafted convenience with a commitment to wellbeing. From grain bowls, salads, wraps, sandwiches, smoothies and more, every menu item is designed to energize every lifestyle. More than just a restaurant, CRISP & GREEN has become a wellness hub where guests gather to fuel body and mind. To celebrate the Chaska opening, CRISP & GREEN is offering a Grand Opening Free Food event from 10:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. on Friday, November 6, where guests can enjoy a complimentary salad, grain bowl or wrap. Recipients must download the CRISP & GREEN app and scan their CRISP Rewards account at checkout to receive their free entree [one per guest]. As part of its mission to empower healthier communities, CRISP & GREEN will also host a free Wellness Series event on Saturday, November 7, at 9:00 a.m. Attendees will meet at the restaurant for a group workout led by local CRISP Fit Coach Bailey Braccini. The first 50 attendees will receive exclusive CRISP & GREEN merch and wellness gifts from best-in-class brands like Lululemon, Isopure, Olipop, and more and the opportunity to enter to win a Peloton bike! Reserve your spot now by visiting crispandgreen.com/events. The event will be followed by CRISP & GREEN food sampling and premium wellness brand activations at the restaurant. Located at 122 Pioneer Trail, the Chaska CRISP & GREEN will be open daily from 10:30 a.m.

articles.titleKo: Döner Haus to Open First Long Island Location
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Döner Haus, the German-style Döner concept bringing one of Europe’s favorite street foods to the U.S., is opening its first Long Island location in Wantagh on Friday, Nov. 13. Located at 3336 Jerusalem Ave., the new restaurant will serve the brand’s signature Döner Sandwiches, Döner Wraps and Döner Boxes, loaded with freshly sliced, filler-free, 100% Zabiha Halal meats, fresh vegetables and creamy garlic sauce. The formula is simple: do one thing and do it right. In this case, make a Döner you’ll have dreams about. The Wantagh restaurant is owned and operated by franchise partner Hamza Jalili, marking his second Döner Haus following the opening of his Bayside location in Queens. A third restaurant in Garden City Park is expected in the coming months. Long Island, consider this the start of a very tasty habit. “We’re proud to bring some German flair to Long Island and show the community what makes Döner Haus special: We do one thing and we do it right.,” said Hamza Jalili, owner of Döner Haus Wantagh. “We’ve seen guests in Bayside come in curious and return as regulars, so we’re excited to see that same energy in Wantagh.” THIS IS HOW WE DÖNER Döner Haus started with a craving that wouldn’t quit. After moving to New York, German-born founder Nikolaus von Solodkoff missed the Döner Kebabs he grew up eating, so he stopped looking and started building, founding Döner Haus in New York City in 2023. Beginning in the East Village and opening to franchising opportunities the following year, Nikolaus set out to bring this crave-worthy concept across the U.S. With roots in Germany’s Turkish immigrant communities, German-style Döner brings together meat cooked on a vertical rotisserie, Turkish bread, fresh vegetables and plenty of sauce. In Germany, it’s an everyday favorite for lunch breaks, dinner on the go and the inevitable late-night craving. Döner Haus is here to make it just as much of a habit in the U.S. No passport required. YOUR DÖNER. YOUR BUSINESS Guests can choose chicken, beef or a mix of both, tucked into a crispy Turkish pide pocket. The Döner Sandwich and Döner Wrap come with red cabbage, lettuce, tomatoes, onions and signature garlic sauce. Prefer a fork? Döner Boxes offer a choice of fries, rice or salad, from a loaded comfort-food fix to a lighter, protein-packed lunch, with every meal delivering 53 grams of protein. While others continue to add to their menus, Döner Haus keeps things simple with an easy-to-navigate menu that makes ordering a breeze, even at midnight. Your call. Nein regrets. GOOD DÖNER GETS AROUND With more than 50 franchise commitments nationwide, Döner Haus is giving the usual lunch order some competition. Its expansion is backed by efficient kitchens and a proprietary operating platform connecting ordering, inventory, reporting and franchisee support. AI-powered tools help answer customer calls and turn daily operating data into practical guidance, giving franchise partners more time to focus on food and service. The next big thing in fast-casual is just getting started. For more information, visit doner.haus. For the latest openings, updates and a little giggle, follow the brand on Instagram at @realdonerhaus and TikTok at @realdonerhaus. Like the brand and want in? articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Salty x Táche limited time menu will be available Available Nov. 13–22 at all Salty locations. The Salty, a national modern donut and coffee brand founded by Amanda Pizarro with more than 20 locations across the U.S., has announced a partnership with Táche, the original pistachio milk founded by Roxana Saidi. Launching at all Salty locations on Friday, Nov. 13, the partnership’s limited-edition fall drink offerings coincide with The Salty’s addition of Táche as a plant-based milk offering on its permanent, year-round menu. “I reached out to Táche because I loved the product and felt an immediate connection to what they were building,” said Amanda Pizarro, founder and chief brand officer of The Salty. “As a fellow founder, I really respect the care they put into their ingredients and the way they’ve built the brand. We’re obsessive about what goes into our coffee at The Salty, so bringing Táche behind our bar felt like a natural fit. And instead of simply adding a new milk, we wanted to make a little more of it, with a full menu and experience to celebrate.” Available Nov. 13–22 at all Salty locations, The Salty x Táche limited time menu will feature two specialty items, including: Pistachio Orgeat Latte ($8): Available as an espresso or matcha latte, the drink features house-made pistachio and orgeat syrup and Táche Original Barista Pistachio Milk topped with pistachio and vanilla swirled whip and pistachio crunch. Pistachio Tres Leches Donut ($5.25): The Salty’s signature 24-hour brioche donut soaked in Táche Original Barista Pistachio Milk, bottom dipped in pistachio white chocolate and topped with torched vanilla bean meringue and caramelized pistachios. To celebrate the launch, The Salty’s Georgetown location in Washington D.C. will host a one-day pop-up on Saturday, Nov. 7 giving guests early access to the limited time Táche menu and exclusive co-branded merch. On Friday, Nov. 13 through Sunday, Nov. 15, the first 10 guests to order the Táche drink and donut pairing at every Salty location will receive an exclusive key chain or bandana gift with their purchase. Táche will be available to order year-round at all Salty locations. “The Salty has built something really special by bringing creativity and an extraordinary level of care to both its coffee and culinary offerings,” said Roxana Saidi, founder and CEO of Táche. “We’ve long believed pistachio milk deserves a place behind the bar alongside the very best ingredients, and this partnership is such a natural expression of that. We’re thrilled to bring Táche to The Salty’s cafés nationwide, kicking things off with a deliciously creative menu that celebrates everything pistachio has to offer.” Known today for its signature 24-hour brioche donuts, meticulously sourced coffee program and warm hospitality, The Salty was founded by Amanda Pizarro in 2015 with a Miami pop-up in a vintage camper. The brand has since grown to more than 20 locations across eight states and recently developed a line of bottled, clean-label coffee syrups. The quarter began with consumer concerns surrounding Cyclospora and fresh produce consumption, which reduced CAVA’s same-restaurant sales by an estimated 150 basis points. The food safety issues were not directly connected to the chain, but they temporarily affected customer behavior across the category. Higher gasoline prices created another obstacle following Labor Day, contributing to uneven traffic patterns before conditions improved toward the end of September. CAVA did not introduce additional promotions or make significant changes to its operations in response to the produce concerns. articles.title: Wendy’s Rejects $1.4 Billion Takeover Bid, Adopts Poison Pill
articles.titleKo: Wendy’s Rejects $1.4 Billion Takeover Bid, Adopts Poison Pill
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Wendy's five-part comeback strategy focuses on menu quality and value, marketing, restaurant operations, digital engagement, and restaurant-level growth and profitability. Wendy’s announced Thursday that it rejected a proposal from an investor group led by billionaire Nelson Peltz’s Trian Fund Management and adopted a shareholder rights plan, otherwise known as a poison pill, to protect itself from a hostile takeover. An independent committee of its board unanimously rejected the $7.35-per-share cash offer from Trian, Flynn Group, BlueFive Capital, and Sixth Street Partners. The proposal, which valued Wendy’s equity at approximately $1.4 billion, sought to acquire all outstanding shares not already owned by the investor group. After reviewing the proposal with its financial and legal advisors, the committee concluded that the offer substantially undervalued Wendy’s and failed to reflect the company’s long-term earnings potential. “The Independent Committee thoroughly evaluated this Proposal and unanimously concluded that it substantially undervalues Wendy’s standalone prospects and long-term earnings potential,” Art Winkleblack, chairman of Wendy’s board and a member of the independent committee, said in a statement. “Our confidence rests firmly in [CEO] Bob Wright’s proven track record of seasoned industry leadership, including restaurant business turnarounds. We believe in Bob and his executive team’s ability to execute on the plan they recently presented to our franchisees at the 2026 Wendy’s convention.” The rejection comes shortly after the investor group submitted its nonbinding proposal, which represented an approximately 20 percent premium to Wendy’s stock price before the offer. Trian and related parties own approximately 16.3 percent of Wendy’s, while Flynn Group operates more than 340 Wendy’s restaurants. Meanwhile, the shareholder rights plan is designed to make it harder for an investor to take control of Wendy’s without paying shareholders a fair price. The brand said it adopted the measure partly because the investor group refused to agree to restrictions that would have limited its ability to pursue a takeover. The company is instead backing its newly announced Dave’s Way turnaround strategy, introduced alongside its Q3 earnings results. Led by Wright, the five-part strategy focuses on menu quality and value, marketing, restaurant operations, digital engagement, and restaurant-level growth and profitability. Wendy’s has also established a Strategic Activation Office to coordinate implementation across the franchise system. Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs are serving as financial advisors to the independent committee, while Simpson Thacher & Bartlett is providing legal counsel. Kirkland & Ellis is advising Wendy’s. The decision follows a similar move by Dine Brands , parent of Applebee’s, IHOP, and Fuzzy’s Taco Shop, which recently rejected a $39-per-share takeover proposal from Arkhouse Management and Cobblers Cove Capital. Dine also adopted a shareholder rights plan after determining that the offer substantially undervalued the company.
