articles.title: How Angry Crab Shack is Navigating a 45 Percent Drop in Alaska’s Snow Crab Quota
articles.titleKo: How Angry Crab Shack is Navigating a 45 Percent Drop in Alaska’s Snow Crab Quota
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Angry Crab Shack operates 28 restaurants across the U.S. and U.K. Alaska’s snow crab supply is tightening again, and that’s creating another challenge for seafood restaurants already navigating unpredictable costs and availability. The state’s snow crab quota for the 2026–27 season dropped roughly 45 percent, from 9.3 million pounds to 5.1 million pounds. Meanwhile, increased quotas for Tanner and red king crab are giving operators alternatives as they evaluate purchasing decisions and menu pricing. Angry Crab Shack, which operates 28 restaurants across the U.S. and U.K., has been preparing for these fluctuations by expanding its sourcing relationships, securing longer-term purchasing agreements, and offering alternative crab varieties. The company has also kept its seafood boil prices unchanged for the past 18 months despite volatility in the market. FSR magazine spoke with Angry Crab Shack president and CFO Andy Diamond about navigating seafood shortages, protecting franchisee profitability, maintaining value for customers, and preparing for continued uncertainty in 2027. 1. Alaska’s snow crab quota has dropped roughly 45 percent this season. What does that reduction mean for Angry Crab Shack, and how are you preparing for potential supply shortages and price increases? Though numbers for snow crab look different in Alaska this upcoming season, it’s not entirely unexpected as numerous closures have affected the fisheries since 2021. In 2022, for instance, Bering Sea snow crabs were designated as “overfished,” prompting a two-year closure for the fishery. Though now reopened, the shifts in Alaska’s snow crab fisheries led Angry Crab Shack to turn to fisheries in Newfoundland, Canada, which operate under an entirely different fishing season from Alaska, beginning in April instead of October. In 2026, the Canadian fisheries caught 61,000 tons, or 134 million pounds of snow crab, which helped Angry Crab Shack secure a consistent supply and lock in prices until February 2027. The quota was reduced 3 percent from 2025 and if in April, the Newfoundland snow crab fisheries’ quotas go down, I think there will be enough snow crab, plus the increased availability of Tanner [crab], to meet our demand, provided you’re giving yourself options and you’re planning ahead. 2. What role are direct supplier relationships and longer-term purchasing agreements playing in protecting the business? In the past, we approved all purchases of volatile seafood items, but over the past few years Angry Crab Shack has taken control over procurement of shrimp, snow crab, and king crab. We now handle all supplier contact, process all bids from suppliers, and have more control over pricing for all markets. We are still able to control overall pricing by utilizing master sales agreements (MSAs) with the firm’s main supplier and distributor, Houston, Texas based wholesale distributor Sysco. It’s a benefit we pass on to our potential franchise partners. When buying a franchise, you’re simply not purchasing the name, the recipes and operational system, you’re buying down your risk by benefiting from the purchasing power of a national brand verses a single unit restaurant. 3. With Tanner crab quotas nearly tripling and red king crab quotas rising, are you considering shifting more of your purchasing toward those varieties? articles.title: After Fox Restaurant Concepts, Sam Fox is Authoring a New Kind of Hospitality
articles.titleKo: After Fox Restaurant Concepts, Sam Fox is Authoring a New Kind of Hospitality
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Sam Fox’s name is synonymous with excellence in the restaurant world. The acclaimed entrepreneur went from a college dropout to opening nearly 200 restaurants across the country over the past three decades. Having been nominated for more than a dozen James Beard Awards, Fox built and sold one of the country’s most admired culinary portfolios through Fox Restaurant Concepts (FRC), creating more than 20 brands like True Food Kitchen, The Henry, Flower Child, and North Italia. He sold FRC to The Cheesecake Factory in October 2019 for $353 million , when the group had almost 50 restaurants across eight states. Since then, FRC has grown to 13 concepts with more than 100 locations nationwide, plus 52 North Italia locations. Now, seven years after selling his company, Fox officially announced he was stepping away from FRC on Thursday. His last day was October 30. “It’s hard to sell your business and be partners with the people you sell your business to for this long,” he admits, adding that his departure was the result of a gradual, year-by-year transition rather than a fixed timetable set at the sale. As the business grew, the company built a transition team to manage its next stage, and he and the ownership discussed his timing over the past year. Though the transition was planned and agreed upon years in advance, it marks an important milestone for the restaurateur and his career path as he turns his full attention to the luxury lifestyle hotel and independent restaurant realm. “The timing coincides with the success of the hotel and some of the growth I want to do outside of Fox Restaurants,” he notes. “We’re really excited for the future, for what’s ahead for FRC, and equally, if not even more excited for what our new organization is going to do.” In 2021, Sam Fox opened The Twelve Thirty Club—a multi-level dining and entertainment destination inspired by the supper clubs of the Prohibition era—in partnership with celebrity Justin Timberlake in Nashville, Tennessee. Fox created Author & Edit Hospitality in 2021 with the debut opening of The Twelve Thirty Club—a multi-level dining and entertainment destination inspired by the supper clubs of the Prohibition era—in partnership with celebrity Justin Timberlake in Nashville, Tennessee. He then created his first hotel, The Global Ambassador in Phoenix , in December 2023. “Opening The Global Ambassador put me in a world I had never been in before. After spending my entire career in restaurants, suddenly I was a first-time hotelier, earning a MICHELIN Key in our first year and every year since. And I loved it,” Fox notes. “It reminded me how much I still have to learn and how much more there is to create. In a lot of ways, I feel like I’m starting all over again, only this time with nearly 30 years of experience behind me. And that’s what makes it so exciting.” His shift into the hotel side of hospitality stemmed from his past frustrating experience opening a restaurant inside a hotel, where third-party operators worked to operate the various parts from the restaurants to the valet and spa. “I looked around and everyone was working in different silos, and it was really draining and taxing on the guests and really not great for employees either. And I said, ‘This model is broken,’” he recalls. “The level of caring and the level of thoughtfulness that went into the employees and to the guests was diluted, and I didn’t want to be part of that anymore.” That was the inspiration for Fox to set out to create his own hotel—one that he would create, develop, and operate independently to ensure cohesiveness and a better experience for all. “I’m not going to outsource that to a Marriott or a Hyatt or any of the other big companies. articles.originalSummary: Low Wood Bay pastry chef Jibin Thomas created a scale-size gingerbread replica of the popular Lake Windermere hotel in the Lake District which is hosting The Gingerbread House Festival 20–22 November Professional bakers, confectioners and chefs in Cumbria are being urged to compete for £1500 cash prizes by creating show-stopping gingerbread houses. The £1000 winner and £500 runner-up awards – provided by leading wholesale food suppliers Caterite and Bidfood – are supporting The Gingerbread House Festival being held in the Lake District in November. Joanne, Hunter, co-director of Grasmere Gingerbread® and organiser of the event, announced that Caterite is sponsoring the £1000 winner’s prize in the Culinary Professional category of The Gingerbread House Festival. “It is a very generous amount and we are very grateful for their sponsorship,” she said. “Of course, Caterite is already widely-known and respected for championing food, innovation and craftsmanship. “Similarly, the £500 runner-up cash prize from Bidfood is much appreciated and reflects their passion for good food. “I hope that these generous cash awards will encourage culinary professionals from Cumbria to enter The Gingerbread House Festival and give it the wow factor.” Taking place at the Low Wood Bay Resort & Spa overlooking Lake Windermere on the weekend of November 20–22, The Gingerbread House Festival challenges bakers, confectioners and chefs to reimagine the classic gingerbread house design. The event is raising money for Shelter, the housing and homelessness charity. From traditional country cottages, elegant stately homes and global cultural landmarks to famous pieces of brutalist architecture, iconic modes of transport or even ‘emergency’ accommodation, The Gingerbread House Festival will showcase all kinds of ‘gingerbread house’ designs. Beth Evans, Head of Sales at Caterite, said her company was “delighted” to support an event celebrating gingerbread which is an iconic part of Cumbria’s food heritage. “The Gingerbread House Festival brings together an incredible range of talent – from schoolchildren taking their first steps in baking and design through to experienced professionals showcasing their creativity and skill,” she said. Cumbrian baker John Crouch created Ambleside’s famous Bridge House from gingerbread “It’s wonderful to see a competition that inspires people of all ages to get involved and the enthusiasm and imagination shown by the entrants perfectly reflects the spirit of our industry. “That the Gingerbread House Festival is also raising for Shelter, the charity for housing and homelessness, makes it even more worthwhile. Andy Pearson, Head of Business Development at Bidfood, was “delighted” to help bring “such a fantastic event” to the Lake District. “At Bidfood, we’re passionate about supporting the businesses, communities and charities that make Cumbria such a special place,” he said. “Our relationship with Low Wood Bay is a long-standing one, and it’s fantastic to see that partnership continue through to The Gingerbread House Festival. “We look forward to seeing it become a standout event in the Cumbrian calendar.” To enter and find out more about The Gingerbread House Festival please visit: www.gingerbreadhousefestival.com

articles.titleKo: Pague Menos amplia lucro em 19,5% no 3T26; vendas digitais crescem 32,8%
articles.originalSummary: A Pague Menos ( PGMN3 ) registrou lucro líquido ajustado de R$ 96,3 milhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, crescimento de 19,5% em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado. O resultado , divulgado ao mercado nesta quarta-feira, 4, foi favorecido pelo controle de despesas, pela melhora da margem bruta e pela redução dos custos financeiros. A companhia também registrou avanço de 32,8% nas vendas digitais, que contribuíram para sustentar o crescimento da operação em um cenário de desaceleração do mercado farmacêutico. A receita bruta somou R$ 4,429 bilhões, alta de 6,9% na comparação anual. Embora positiva, a expansão ficou abaixo dos 9,3% registrados no segundo trimestre e dos 14,4% do primeiro trimestre de 2026. A companhia atribui a perda de ritmo principalmente às bases de comparação mais elevadas, especialmente dos medicamentos GLP-1, que impulsionaram as vendas ao longo de 2025. O Ebitda ajustado atingiu R$ 278,8 milhões, crescimento de 7,2% em relação ao terceiro trimestre do ano passado. A margem Ebitda permaneceu em 6,3%, enquanto a margem líquida ajustada avançou de 1,9% para 2,2%. No acumulado dos nove primeiros meses de 2026, a receita bruta chegou a R$ 12,916 bilhões, alta de 10%, enquanto o lucro líquido ajustado somou R$ 225,5 milhões, avanço de 46,5%. Controle de despesas e menor custo financeiro sustentam lucro A melhora do resultado da Pague Menos ocorreu mesmo diante de um crescimento mais moderado das vendas. Um dos fatores foi a expansão da margem bruta, que passou de 29,9% para 30% na comparação anual, o maior patamar para um terceiro trimestre desde 2018. O lucro bruto somou R$ 1,327 bilhão, crescimento de 7,2%. Segundo a companhia, o desempenho reflete melhorias nas condições comerciais, especialmente nas categorias de medicamentos genéricos e GLP-1, além de ganhos tributários relacionados ao novo centro de distribuição na Paraíba. A empresa também destacou a manutenção das perdas de estoque em níveis reduzidos, resultado associado à maior eficiência na gestão de mercadorias, com utilização crescente de ferramentas de inteligência artificial. As despesas gerais e administrativas totalizaram R$ 102,8 milhões, redução de 3,3% em relação ao mesmo trimestre de 2025. A queda foi explicada principalmente por menores provisões para remuneração variável e planos de ações restritas. Já as despesas com vendas cresceram 8,5%, chegando a R$ 946 milhões, pressionadas por custos relacionados à operação do novo centro de distribuição, à expansão da rede e a ajustes no quadro de funcionários. O resultado financeiro também contribuiu para a melhora do lucro. As despesas financeiras líquidas diminuíram 13%, passando de R$ 129,6 milhões para R$ 112,7 milhões. A redução foi favorecida por menores custos com antecipações de recebíveis e pela queda do CDI médio no período. Digital cresce 32,8% e amplia participação nas vendas A estratégia digital permaneceu como uma das principais frentes de crescimento da Pague Menos no terceiro trimestre. As vendas realizadas pelos canais digitais somaram aproximadamente R$ 1,1 bilhão, alta de 32,8% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025. Com isso, a participação desses canais na receita bruta passou de 19,8% para 24,6% em um ano, avanço de 4,8 pontos porcentuais. O crescimento foi impulsionado principalmente pelo aplicativo da companhia, cujas vendas aumentaram 73,2% na comparação anual. O canal concentra cerca de dois terços das vendas de e-commerce da rede. Nos últimos 12 meses, a Pague Menos registrou crescimento de 23% no número de usuários ativos mensais do aplicativo, além de 3,4 milhões de downloads. A companhia também ampliou a base de consumidores que utilizam mais de um canal de compra. Os clientes omnicanal passaram a representar 14,5% da base, crescimento de 2,9 pontos porcentuais em relação ao terceiro trimestre de 2025. articles.title: “O plano cabe no bolso da companhia”, diz Caito Maia sobre reestruturação da Chilli Beans
articles.titleKo: “O plano cabe no bolso da companhia”, diz Caito Maia sobre reestruturação da Chilli Beans
articles.originalSummary: Caito Maia, CEO e fundador da Chilli Beans, publicou um vídeo nas redes sociais para comentar o plano de recuperação extrajudicial da companhia e esclarecer as diferenças em relação à recuperação judicial. Segundo o executivo, o procedimento representa um acordo negociado com os credores e aprovado por eles, com condições de pagamento adequadas à capacidade financeira da empresa. A empresa vai renegociar uma dívida financeira de R$ 340 milhões e prevê receber um aporte de até R$ 50 milhões para financiar a reestruturação e sustentar os próximos passos de crescimento. O plano prevê novos prazos e condições para o pagamento das dívidas com instituições financeiras. Segundo a empresa, fornecedores, funcionários e outros parceiros não estão incluídos na negociação. Maia afirmou que as negociações ocorreram de forma sigilosa durante meses e que a conclusão dessa etapa permite à companhia organizar um fluxo de caixa compatível com seu faturamento e suas possibilidades de pagamento. “A gente fez um plano que vai acontecer, que cabe no bolso da companhia”, disse. O executivo também destacou que o protocolo do plano foi motivo de comemoração interna, por representar um avanço na construção de uma estrutura financeira viável. Na recuperação extrajudicial, a empresa negocia diretamente com seus credores um plano de reestruturação, que pode ser submetido à homologação judicial, conforme os requisitos legais. No vídeo, Caito Maia reafirmou que permanece à frente da Chilli Beans como CEO e mencionou a atuação de André Dela Togna como co-CEO, responsável por comandar as frentes financeira e de reestruturação da empresa. Segundo ele, as mudanças internas começaram há cerca de dois meses e já apresentam resultados positivos. O empresário também aproveitou o vídeo para alertar outros empreendedores sobre a importância de agir rapidamente diante de dificuldades financeiras, especialmente na revisão de despesas e na redução de custos. “Não demorem para tomar decisões, não demorem para diminuir custos, porque isso pode ser fatal. Cada dia que você demora pode ser fatal”, afirmou. Apesar do momento de reorganização financeira, Maia demonstrou otimismo em relação ao futuro da marca e mencionou os preparativos para a comemoração dos 30 anos da Chilli Beans, em 2027. articles.title: Banco Central mantém juros básicos em 13,75% ao ano
articles.titleKo: Banco Central mantém juros básicos em 13,75% ao ano
articles.originalSummary: As tensões em torno do câmbio e do fenômeno climático El Niño fizeram o Banco Central ( BC ) botar o pé no freio. Por unanimidade, o Comitê de Política Monetária (Copom) manteve a Taxa Selic, juros básicos da economia, em 13,75% ao ano. A decisão surpreendeu o mercado financeiro, que esperava um corte de 0,25 ponto percentual. No entanto, uma parte das instituições apostavam na manutenção da taxa. De junho de 2025 a março de 2026, a Selic ficou em 15% ao ano, o maior nível em quase 20 anos. Desde abril, o Copom cortou os juros cinco vezes, num cenário de queda da inflação. No entanto, o agravamento da guerra no Oriente Médio, o início do fenômeno El Niño e a recente instabilidade cambial dificultam o trabalho do órgão. O Copom está desfalcado porque o mandato dos diretores de Organização do Sistema Financeiro, Renato Gomes, e de Política Econômica, Diego Guillen, expirou no fim de 2025. O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ainda não encaminhou as indicações dos substitutos ao Congresso Nacional. Inflação A Selic é o principal instrumento do Banco Central para manter sob controle a inflação oficial, medida pelo Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor Amplo (IPCA). Em outubro, o IPCA-15, prévia do índice oficial ficou em 0,32%, beneficiado pela queda nas contas de luz. No acumulado de 12 meses, o índice subiu de 4,5% para 4,62%, acima do teto da meta de inflação. O Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) divulgará o IPCA cheio de setembro no próximo dia 12. Pelo novo sistema de meta contínua, em vigor desde janeiro de 2025, a meta de inflação que deve ser perseguida pelo BC, definida pelo Conselho Monetário Nacional, é de 3%, com intervalo de tolerância de 1,5 ponto percentual para cima ou para baixo. Ou seja, o limite inferior é 1,5% e o superior é 4,5%. No modelo de meta contínua, a meta passa ser apurada mês a mês, considerando a inflação acumulada em 12 meses. Em novembro de 2026, a inflação desde dezembro de 2025 é comparada com a meta e o intervalo de tolerância. Em dezembro de 2026, o procedimento se repete, com apuração a partir de janeiro de 2026. Dessa forma, a verificação se desloca ao longo do tempo, não ficando mais restrita ao índice fechado de dezembro de cada ano. No último Relatório de Política Monetária, divulgado no fim de setembro pelo Banco Central, a autoridade monetária manteve, em 5,2% a previsão do IPCA em 2026, mas a estimativa será revista, por causa da recente queda da inflação. A próxima edição do documento será divulgada no fim deste mês. As previsões do mercado estão em linha com as da autoridade monetária. De acordo com o boletim Focus, pesquisa semanal com instituições financeiras divulgada pelo BC, a inflação oficial deverá fechar o ano em 5,22%, acima do teto da meta, de 4,5%. Antes do início da guerra no Oriente Médio, as estimativas do mercado estavam em 3,95%. Crédito menos caro A redução da taxa Selic impulsiona a economia. Isso porque juros mais baixos barateiam o crédito e estimulam a produção e o consumo. Por outro lado, taxas menores dificultam o controle da inflação. No último Relatório de Política Monetária, o Banco Central reduziu para 1,8% a previsão de crescimento da economia em 2026. O mercado projeta crescimento um pouco mais baixo. Segundo a última edição do boletim Focus, os analistas econômicos preveem expansão de 1,76% do PIB em 2026. Há quatro semanas, a estimativa estava em 1,85% A taxa básica de juros é usada nas negociações de títulos públicos no Sistema Especial de Liquidação e Custódia (Selic) e serve de referência para as demais taxas de juros da economia. Ao reajustá-la para cima, o Banco Central segura o excesso de demanda que pressiona os preços, porque juros mais altos encarecem o crédito e estimulam a poupança. Ao reduzir os juros básicos, o Copom barateia o crédito e incentiva a produção e o consumo, mas enfraquece o controle da inflação. articles.originalSummary: O decreto que regulamentará o fim da escala de trabalho 6×1 deve sair na próxima segunda-feira, 9, disse nesta quarta-feira, 4, o ministro do Trabalho e Emprego, Luiz Marinho. O texto estabelecerá diretrizes para a organização das jornadas e garantir pelo menos oito folgas por mês aos trabalhadores. Seguindo Marinho, o decreto será discutido com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva nesta quinta-feira (5) e deverá orientar a implementação das novas regras por meio de negociações coletivas. A regulamentação também deverá permitir flexibilidade na organização das escalas, desde que sejam respeitados os direitos previstos na Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) que extinguiu o modelo de seis dias de trabalho para um de descanso. Decreto Segundo Marinho, o decreto terá como objetivo coordenar a adoção das diferentes escalas de trabalho nos setores econômicos, sem comprometer os direitos dos empregados nem o funcionamento das empresas. “Soltaremos o decreto regulamentador para trazer o processo coordenado para a implantação das várias escalas que cada setor pretende implantar, sempre respeitando o comando da PEC”, afirmou o ministro. A publicação, inicialmente prevista para esta semana, foi adiada após Lula não conseguir realizar o despacho sobre o tema. A expectativa do Ministério do Trabalho é concluir a regulamentação na próxima segunda-feira. Folgas e negociação A proposta prevê que os trabalhadores tenham, no mínimo, oito folgas em um período de 30 dias. A distribuição dos descansos poderá variar conforme as características de cada atividade, desde que respeitadas as condições estabelecidas pela PEC e pelos acordos coletivos. Marinho explicou que a flexibilização poderá permitir diferentes combinações de jornadas semanais, conforme as necessidades de cada setor. “Não tem lista de flexibilidade. A PEC determina dois descansos semanais. A flexibilidade concedida é que essas duas folgas estejam consolidadas dentro do mês”, declarou. O ministro destacou que os acordos coletivos terão papel central na organização das escalas. A prioridade, segundo ele, será a negociação entre empresas e representantes dos trabalhadores, com possibilidade de convenções nacionais que facilitem a adesão dos diferentes estados. A regulamentação também deverá contemplar setores que funcionam continuamente, como atividades de saúde, transporte, segurança e limpeza urbana. Redução da jornada A proposta de mudança na jornada de trabalho prevê a redução gradual da carga horária semanal, atualmente de 44 horas, para 40 horas. De acordo com as informações divulgadas pelo governo, a implementação deverá ocorrer a partir de 15 de dezembro, respeitando as condições estabelecidas na regulamentação. O Congresso Nacional promulgou, em 16 de outubro, a PEC que extingue a escala 6×1 e estabelece uma jornada de cinco dias de trabalho para dois de descanso. Marinho afirmou que o objetivo do governo é garantir a proteção dos trabalhadores durante a transição, sem prejudicar a atividade econômica. A manifestação ocorreu após questionamentos sobre as ideias do economista André Lara Resende, um dos formuladores do Plano Real, que defende mudanças na condução das políticas fiscal e monetária. Marinho afirmou que o presidente Lula deve ter liberdade para ouvir diferentes contribuições, mesmo quando elas divergem das posições defendidas por agentes financeiros. “O que eu acho um absurdo é que qualquer tentativa de discussão que não esteja no quadradinho do chamado mercado da Faria Lima há uma grita contra”, declarou. articles.title: Após proibição das bets, 84,3% das lojas de atacarejo melhoram desempenho, aponta NIQ
articles.titleKo: Após proibição das bets, 84,3% das lojas de atacarejo melhoram desempenho, aponta NIQ
articles.originalSummary: O desempenho do atacarejo ganhou força nas semanas seguintes à proibição das bets no Brasil . Levantamento da NielsenIQ (NIQ) mostra que 84,3% das lojas comparáveis do canal melhoraram a taxa de vendas entre as semanas 41 e 43, período que sucede a medida contra as apostas online. O indicador considera estabelecimentos que tiveram melhora em relação ao desempenho anterior, mesmo que ainda apresentem queda nas vendas. Na semana 43, encerrada em 25 de outubro, o atacarejo registrou crescimento de 7,8% no faturamento e de 2,4% nas unidades vendidas. Foi a terceira semana consecutiva de resultados positivos nos dois indicadores, após duas semanas de retração nas unidades. O levantamento identifica a melhora do canal no período posterior à proibição das bets, mas não estabelece uma relação causal entre a medida e o desempenho das vendas. A análise de mesmas lojas reúne 16.353 estabelecimentos dos canais avaliados. No atacarejo, o faturamento passou de queda de 3,5% nas semanas 39 e 40 para alta de 5,4% nas semanas 41 e 42 e de 5,6% no acumulado das semanas 41 a 43, sempre na comparação com os mesmos períodos de 2025. Nos demais canais, as taxas foram de -1,5%, 2,8% e 2,4%, respectivamente. A melhora no atacarejo chegou a cerca de 9 pontos percentuais, ante 3,9 pontos nos outros formatos. Além das 84,3% de lojas que melhoraram a taxa de vendas, 71,4% dos estabelecimentos de atacarejo registraram crescimento positivo do faturamento nas semanas 41 a 43. Nos demais canais, esse percentual foi de 60,7%. A melhora também aparece na análise das dez redes apresentadas no levantamento. Entre as bandeiras, a parcela de lojas que melhoraram a taxa de vendas variou de 93,3% a 100%. Os avanços ficaram entre 8,2 e 22,2 pontos percentuais, na comparação entre os blocos das semanas 39 e 40 e das semanas 41 a 43. Atacarejo mantém crescimento nas vendas Na semana 43, o alimentar de autosserviço registrou alta de 4,8% no faturamento, enquanto as unidades vendidas ficaram praticamente estáveis, com variação de -0,1%. No canal farma, os resultados foram de 7,2% em valor e 3,5% em unidades. No atacarejo, o crescimento das unidades perdeu intensidade ao longo das últimas semanas, passando de 5,5% na semana 41 para 3,0% na semana 42 e 2,4% na semana 43. Apesar da desaceleração, o canal permaneceu no campo positivo. O levantamento também identificou mudanças na composição das compras de alimentos. Entre as semanas 36 e 43, o preço de uma cesta fixa de produtos comuns aos períodos subiu 0,31% no conjunto de autosserviço alimentar e atacarejo. Já o indicador de mix dentro das categorias ficou em 2,96%. No atacarejo, a cesta fixa avançou 0,65%, enquanto o indicador de mix foi de 2,61%. A cesta fixa mede a variação de preço de uma mesma composição de produtos. O indicador de mix mantém os preços de referência constantes e identifica mudanças na participação dos itens dentro das categorias. O resultado positivo aponta maior peso de produtos de preço mais alto, como marcas, versões ou embalagens que exigem maior desembolso por unidade. Na comparação entre as semanas 42 e 43, a cesta fixa do alimentar subiu 0,55% no conjunto de autosserviço e atacarejo, enquanto o mix ficou em 1,94%. No atacarejo, os resultados foram de 0,57% e 0,71%, respectivamente. A mudança na composição aparece com mais clareza em refrigerantes e cervejas. O café não acompanhou o mesmo padrão. Melhora supera a maior parte das janelas históricas A comparação histórica da NIQ mostra que a melhora da taxa de vendas do painel total superou a observada em 93% dos 103 períodos analisados. Já o avanço adicional do atacarejo em relação aos demais canais foi maior do que o registrado em 94% das janelas históricas. O teste compara blocos de duas semanas com blocos de três semanas, cada um em relação ao período correspondente do ano anterior. Os percentuais indicam a posição do resultado no histórico e não representam probabilidades de que a melhora tenha sido causada pela proibição das apostas online.

articles.title: Distrito Federal lidera ranking de interesse pela Black Friday no Google Brasil
articles.titleKo: Distrito Federal lidera ranking de interesse pela Black Friday no Google Brasil
articles.originalSummary: A Black Friday de 2026 ocorre em 27 de novembro, mas a busca pelo tema já movimenta a internet. Segundo estudo do RecargaPay com dados do Google Brasil, o Distrito Federal lidera o ranking de pesquisas pelo termo “Black Friday” entre setembro de 2025 e agosto de 2026. São Paulo aparece em segundo lugar, seguido por Santa Catarina, em terceiro. Rio de Janeiro e Rio Grande do Sul ocupam a quarta e a quinta posições, respectivamente. Paraná, Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo, Goiás e Mato Grosso do Sul completam a lista. DF lidera ranking de interesse pela Black Friday A pesquisa considera o volume de buscas proporcional a cada 100 mil habitantes, com base na população de cada Estado. Os dados não refletem, portanto, intenções de compra ou comportamentos para além do ambiente digital. Vendas online ganham espaço no comércio brasileiro A participação das vendas online no comércio brasileiro também avançou. Segundo o Indicador de Vendas Online da Fundação Getulio Vargas, por meio do Instituto Brasileiro de Economia (FGV-IBRE), as vendas pela internet representaram 18,7% do volume total do comércio no terceiro trimestre de 2025. O resultado foi 1,3 ponto percentual superior ao do trimestre anterior e 4,8 pontos percentuais acima do registrado no mesmo período de 2024. Na mesma análise, 70,2% dos consumidores afirmaram comprar pela internet frequentemente ou de vez em quando. A decisão de compra, no entanto, também é influenciada por fatores como preço, frete, confiança na loja e segurança. Pagamento digital exige atenção a golpes A escolha do meio de pagamento depende do valor da compra, das condições oferecidas pela loja e da capacidade de pagamento de cada consumidor. O Pix permite transferências instantâneas e pode ser uma alternativa prática para quem deseja pagar à vista. O cartão de crédito, por sua vez, permite parcelar compras quando essa opção está disponível. As carteiras digitais e os aplicativos financeiros também podem reunir diferentes meios de pagamento e disponibilizar recursos para organizar as despesas. Já o Pix parcelado exige atenção, pois, quando oferecido por uma instituição financeira, pode envolver uma operação de crédito com juros. A praticidade das transações eletrônicas não elimina os riscos de golpes. Para reduzir a possibilidade de fraude, o consumidor deve acessar o site oficial da loja, conferir a reputação do vendedor e desconfiar de ofertas muito abaixo dos preços praticados no mercado. O Banco Central orienta que vítimas de golpes envolvendo Pix procurem imediatamente sua instituição financeira para contestar a transação e solicitar a análise pelo Mecanismo Especial de Devolução (MED), quando aplicável. O pedido pode ser feito em até 80 dias após a operação, mas a devolução não é garantida. Ela depende da análise do caso e da existência de recursos disponíveis nas contas envolvidas. McDonald's U.S. same-store sales dropped 0.2 percent in Q3. McDonald’s is preparing another major push to win back value-conscious customers in the U.S., with new affordable menu options, expanded digital deals, and restaurant improvements expected to drive stronger performance in 2027. The burger giant reported a 0.2 percent decline in domestic same-store sales during the third quarter, although performance improved as the period progressed. Comparable sales turned positive in September after declining slightly in July and August, offering early evidence that recent changes to the company’s value and marketing strategies are resonating with customers. Globally, same-store sales increased 1.5 percent, and system sales grew 4 percent. International markets continued to outperform the U.S., supported by value platforms, menu innovation, and marketing campaigns. READ MORE : Is ‘Deep Value’ Done in QSR? What McDonald’s New Menu Focus Reveals About What’s Next McDonald’s Unveils Sweeping Plan to Win More Traffic McDonald’s Plans $8.5 Billion in Franchisee Support Under New Growth Strategy CEO Chris Kempczinski said the company is encouraged by improvements in domestic traffic during September and October, but additional work is necessary to restore consistent sales growth. A major priority is addressing what McDonald’s considers the missing component of its value strategy. The company believes its existing meal bundles and everyday menu prices are competitive, but entry-level offerings have not adequately served customers seeking the lowest-priced options. Last week, McDonald’s began an eight-week test of two affordable menu structures across approximately 1,900 restaurants in several U.S. regions. One features mix-and-match bundles that allow customers to select combinations of products. The other provides fixed bundles with predetermined items at attractive prices. Franchisees operating another 4,000 restaurants have independently introduced similar offerings ahead of the formal test results. Combined, the initiatives cover more than 40 percent of the domestic system. McDonald’s plans to evaluate customer response, incremental traffic, sales, and franchisee economics before introducing a national program in early 2027. “Particularly for that low-income consumer, they’re looking for great entry-level value, and we have not had that in place to the level that we are satisfied with,” Kempczinski said. The initiative builds on the company’s existing $5 and $6 meal deals and Extra Value Meals, which returned more than a year ago. Unit sales of the chain’s leading Extra Value Meals have increased approximately 7 percent year-over-year, according to CFO Ian Borden. Recent promotions included a $5 Sausage McMuffin with Egg meal and an $8 Big Mac meal. Those offerings helped improve traffic and average checks during the quarter. McDonald’s also shifted marketing investments toward its established value platforms and restored certain digital promotions that had previously been reduced. Offers such as a $2 breakfast sandwich and free fries with a minimum $1 purchase helped attract additional transactions from loyalty members and customers who had stopped visiting regularly. Borden said the initial response exceeded expectations for incremental traffic and sales, helping reverse negative trends experienced during the second quarter and early third quarter. The importance of those promotions extends across McDonald’s digital ecosystem. The company has more than 45 million U.S. loyalty members, with loyalty participants accounting for nearly 30 percent of its customer base. Customers typically increase their visit frequency approximately 2.5 times during the first 12 months after joining the loyalty program. articles.title: CVS Health vai dividir operações e criar duas empresas independentes
articles.titleKo: CVS Health vai dividir operações e criar duas empresas independentes
articles.originalSummary: A CVS Health anunciou nesta quarta-feira, 4, que pretende se dividir em duas empresas independentes, de capital aberto, separando suas operações de soluções em saúde e benefícios da rede de farmácias e serviços de atendimento. A conclusão da operação está prevista para o primeiro semestre de 2028. A primeira companhia reunirá Aetna, CVS Caremark, CVS Specialty, Oak Street Health e Signify Health, formando uma empresa de soluções em saúde. A segunda, que manterá o nome CVS Pharmacy, concentrará cerca de 9 mil farmácias nos Estados Unidos, serviços de entrega de medicamentos, a rede MinuteClinic, incluindo atendimento virtual, e a plataforma tecnológica Health100. A divisão também dará maior autonomia à operação de farmácias para ampliar os serviços oferecidos por seus quase 30 mil farmacêuticos e estabelecer novas parcerias com operadoras de planos de saúde, gestores de benefícios farmacêuticos e fabricantes de medicamentos. Já a companhia de soluções em saúde manterá a integração entre benefícios, serviços farmacêuticos e atendimento médico. O objetivo é combinar essas operações para reduzir custos e melhorar os resultados e a experiência dos pacientes. Segundo comunicado da CVS Health , a tecnologia será uma frente comum às duas empresas. Ambas continuarão investindo no Health100, plataforma que deverá oferecer produtos e serviços baseados em inteligência artificial (IA) para enfrentar desafios relacionados a custos, acesso e experiência no sistema de saúde. David Joyner, atual presidente e CEO da CVS Health, comandará a companhia de soluções em saúde. Prem Shah, atual presidente do grupo, será o CEO da CVS Pharmacy. Outros nomes para cargos de liderança e conselhos de administração serão anunciados posteriormente. Segundo a CVS Health, a separação busca dar maior foco estratégico às operações, ampliar a agilidade para inovar e melhorar a eficiência. Cada empresa terá estrutura de capital independente e autonomia para definir investimentos e prioridades. Com a conclusão da operação, os atuais acionistas da CVS Health terão participação nas duas companhias. Ambas deverão manter grau de investimento, geração robusta de fluxo de caixa e capacidade para distribuir dividendos. A separação ainda depende de condições usuais, incluindo aprovação final do conselho de administração e registro junto à autoridade reguladora do mercado de capitais dos Estados Unidos ( SEC ). Até a conclusão do processo, a CVS Health continuará operando normalmente. Segundo a companhia, não haverá interrupção no fornecimento de medicamentos, nos atendimentos ou nos serviços prestados a clientes e pacientes. articles.title: Nestlé e Kibon concentram disputa por ofertas de sorvetes no Brasil
articles.titleKo: Nestlé e Kibon concentram disputa por ofertas de sorvetes no Brasil
articles.originalSummary: O mercado brasileiro de sorvetes registrou aumento de 35% na quantidade de ofertas entre janeiro e setembro de 2026, em comparação com o mesmo período de 2024. O crescimento foi ainda mais expressivo nos meses tradicionalmente mais frios: entre junho e agosto, as promoções avançaram 78%. Os dados são de um levantamento da Shopping Brasil, empresa especializada no monitoramento de ofertas no varejo. Entre as marcas, Nestlé e Kibon concentram a disputa pela liderança nas ofertas de sorvetes em potes acima de 600 ml. A Nestlé manteve a primeira posição, com 24,7% de participação em 2026, mas perdeu 10,6 pontos percentuais em relação a 2024. Já a Kibon avançou 6,3 pontos percentuais e alcançou 24%, reduzindo a diferença entre as duas marcas para apenas 0,7 ponto percentual. A Nobrelli também ampliou sua presença promocional, com ganho de 3,4 pontos percentuais, chegando a 9,7% das ofertas monitoradas nesse segmento. “A busca por produtos de maior valor agregado, formatos individuais e opções alinhadas à saudabilidade também faz parte desse cenário”, explica Renata González, sócia e diretora Comercial da Shopping Brasil. Picolés e embalagens menores ganham espaço Apesar da liderança dos potes acima de 600 ml, que concentraram 65,5% das ofertas entre janeiro e setembro de 2026, o formato perdeu 6,6 pontos percentuais de participação em relação a 2024. Na contramão, os picolés avançaram seis pontos percentuais, passando de 8,7% para 14,7% das ofertas. Os potes de até 600 ml também ganharam espaço, com aumento de 3,6 pontos percentuais, alcançando 14,2%. Regionalmente, o Centro-Oeste registrou a maior expansão percentual, com alta de 66% no volume de ofertas entre janeiro e setembro de 2026, na comparação com o mesmo período de 2024. A região contabilizou 8.069 promoções. O Nordeste aparece na sequência, com crescimento de 58% e 11.639 ofertas. O Sudeste permanece na liderança em volume, com 20.085 ofertas, apesar do avanço mais moderado, de 21%. No Sul, foram registradas 9.249 ofertas, alta de 25%, enquanto o Norte contabilizou 1.277, crescimento de 28%. Atacado e farmácias ampliam participação Os supermercados concentraram 50,3% das ofertas de sorvetes em 2026, mas perderam 4,5 pontos percentuais de participação em relação a 2024. O atacado avançou 2,3 pontos percentuais, chegando a 22,4%. Os hipermercados, por sua vez, registraram retração de 9,6 pontos percentuais, encerrando o período com 14,6% de participação. As farmácias responderam por 12,6% das ofertas monitoradas. Na comunicação promocional, as redes sociais ampliaram sua participação de 55,6% em 2024 para 66,3% em 2026. Os tabloides também avançaram, passando de 26,8% para 28,6%. De acordo com Renata González, os resultados apontam para uma categoria com maior atividade promocional e mudanças na distribuição regional, nos canais de venda e nos formatos de produtos anunciados. O crescimento das ofertas durante o inverno indica uma movimentação de fabricantes e varejistas para ampliar a presença dos sorvetes ao longo do ano. articles.title: Nash & Smashed Picks Qu to Fuel Expansion
articles.titleKo: Nash & Smashed Picks Qu to Fuel Expansion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Nash & Smashed, the fast-growing franchise known for hand-smashed burgers and halal-certified Nashville hot chicken, has selected Qu’s intelligent commerce platform to run its restaurants as it expands. Founded less than three years ago, the brand now has 35 franchise locations with more in the pipeline, including new markets in Richmond and Delaware. Each Qu-powered location runs on one connected platform that covers front-counter POS, self-order kiosks, kitchen display, first-party online ordering, third-party delivery, and Qu Pay. The connected data platform matters for a brand where about 40 percent of orders are digital, and most of those come through its own website. “It’s not a POS, it’s an ERP solution for everything,” said Lamaan Malik, Chief Operating Officer at Nash & Smashed. “Every time we needed something customized, from tiered menus to how orders hit the kitchen, the Qu team turned it around fast. We’re not just running stores on Qu; we’re growing the business on it.” Nash & Smashed CEO M.N. Abbasi first saw Qu as a guest. Impressed with how it worked, he told his team to skip the usual short list of POS providers and talk to Qu. After a single product demo, the Nash & Smashed team was ready to move. Nash & Smashed had been on a plug-and-play POS that installed quickly but left gaps. It didn’t track leakage or theft, offered little menu or upsell flexibility, and had limited reporting. Qu goes much deeper, and the brand chose that depth on purpose. To make that depth easy to adopt, Qu paired Nash & Smashed with a dedicated team who built the menus, handled customization requests, and guided the franchise through each launch, for a smooth change management process. In Qu’s lab, franchisees could test the system, ask questions, and shape the rollout before their own stores went live. Owners now get detailed performance reports and analytics across their stores. Qu’s flexible menu tools let Nash & Smashed design tiered offers that weren’t possible before. The previous system supported one meal size and a flat add-on. With Qu, cross-sells and upsells are easier. Early results show meaningfully higher check sizes, with new kiosk-led locations seeing check averages up to 70 percent higher than the brand’s older stores. “Nash & Smashed is building a big brand fast, and they need a partner who can keep up without cutting corners,” said Steve Melamed, Chief Revenue Officer at Qu. “Our team works side by side with franchisees to configure the platform around how they run their business, so every new store opens ready to perform. Seeing their guests trade up on the kiosk and their owners get a real view into kitchen performance is what serving smarter looks like. We’re proud to be part of their growth.” “Once I saw the functionality, I stopped the sales rep in the middle of the meeting and said, ‘I’m sold,’ Malik added. “The onboarding process was the most detailed I’ve seen, but the team made the whole experience easy. If you’re a growing brand thinking about Qu, close your eyes and just say yes.” Nash & Smashed is also looking at Qu for future concepts as its franchise system grows with new franchises across the country. New Nash & Smashed restaurants will be opening on Qu. Hungry to see it in action? Stop by Nash & Smashed in Arlington, Pimmit Hills, or Virginia Beach, Va., and order a hand-smashed burger or Nashville hot chicken right from the Qu kiosk, with Hyattsville, MD, coming soon. Find a location near you at nashandsmashed.com. The post Nash & Smashed Picks Qu to Fuel Expansion appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Bares e restaurantes são o 2º maior empregador de jovens no Brasil, com 250 mil contratações
articles.titleKo: Bares e restaurantes são o 2º maior empregador de jovens no Brasil, com 250 mil contratações
articles.originalSummary: O setor de bares e restaurantes contratou 250,9 mil jovens de 18 a 24 anos com carteira assinada entre janeiro e junho de 2026. O resultado coloca o segmento em segundo lugar em contratações nessa faixa etária entre 52 atividades econômicas, atrás apenas do comércio varejista, aponta a Associação Brasileira de Bares e Restaurantes ( Abrasel ) com base nos dados do Novo Caged, do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego. Os jovens responderam por 36,1% das 694,6 mil admissões do setor no semestre, contra 30,3% nos demais setores analisados. Na prática, o segmento contrata proporcionalmente 19% mais jovens. O varejo lidera em números absolutos porque é o maior empregador do grupo. Foram 2,2 milhões de admissões no semestre, mais de três vezes o volume de bares e restaurantes. Na proporção, os dois setores ficam praticamente empatados, com 36,4% dos contratados pelo varejo sendo jovens, ante 36,1% em bares e restaurantes. A participação desse público cresceu mês a mês. Em janeiro, representava 35,1% das contratações do setor. Em junho, chegou a 36,6%. Retrato regional O padrão se repete em quase todo o País. Em 26 das 27 unidades da federação, bares e restaurantes contratam proporcionalmente mais jovens que os demais setores. Rondônia é a única exceção. O Acre tem a maior participação, com 47,6% dos contratados entre 18 e 24 anos, ante 36,4% nas demais atividades. No Amazonas, o índice foi de 42,7% e, no Distrito Federal, de 40,3%. Nas capitais, a diferença em relação aos demais setores fica mais evidente. Em São Paulo, os jovens representaram 36,9% das contratações do setor, enquanto nas outras atividades o percentual foi de 26,8%. No Rio de Janeiro, foram 35,4%, enquanto nos demais setores chegaram a 25,0%. Em Belém, 36,1%, contra 25,9%. Nas três cidades, a diferença supera 10 pontos percentuais. Sobre o levantamento A Abrasel analisou 14 milhões de admissões registradas no Novo Caged entre janeiro e junho de 2026. O setor de alimentação fora do lar inclui restaurantes, bares, lanchonetes, padarias com predominância de revenda e fornecedores de alimentos preparados para consumo em casa. A comparação considera atividades com características produtivas e ocupacionais semelhantes, como comércio, indústria, agropecuária, alojamento e serviços de apoio a empresas. Já administração pública, educação, saúde e finanças foram excluídas por terem regras próprias de contratação. articles.title: Unilever inaugura hub logístico de 50 mil m² em Itupeva
articles.titleKo: Unilever inaugura hub logístico de 50 mil m² em Itupeva
articles.originalSummary: A Unilever inaugurou seu primeiro hub logístico no Brasil, localizado em Itupeva (SP), com 50 mil m² de área. Considerado um dos armazéns mais automatizados da companhia no mundo, o empreendimento integra um ciclo de investimentos de R$ 145 milhões, iniciado em 2025, para ampliar, modernizar e automatizar a rede logística da empresa no País. Os aportes permitirão aumentar em 40% a capacidade de armazenamento da Unilever no Brasil. O novo empreendimento é o nono centro de distribuição da companhia no País e foi projetado para integrar operações, ampliar a eficiência e atender ao crescimento dos negócios. “O novo hub nos prepara para uma nova etapa de crescimento, elevando nossa eficiência operacional e fortalecendo nossa capacidade de atender clientes em todo o país com mais agilidade. A inovação e a tecnologia são pilares centrais dessa transformação”, afirma Alexandre Camiloti, vice-presidente de Operações da Unilever Brasil. A estrutura utiliza tecnologias da Geek+, incluindo os sistemas ASRS (Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems), com shuttles 4D, e ATLS (Automated Truck Loading System). As soluções automatizam os processos de descarregamento, movimentação, armazenagem e carregamento de mercadorias. Implementadas pela primeira vez pela Unilever na América Latina, as tecnologias permitem dobrar a capacidade de armazenamento na mesma área física, em comparação com centros de distribuição convencionais. Além disso, reduzem em até 60% o tempo necessário para carregar e descarregar produtos. Com movimentação diária de aproximadamente 1,5 mil toneladas, o hub receberá produtos das fábricas de Indaiatuba, Valinhos, Vinhedo e Aguaí, todas no interior paulista. A partir da unidade, será concentrado o abastecimento dos centros de distribuição da Unilever em todo o Brasil, por meio do operador logístico Kuehne + Nagel. A estrutura também busca reduzir a sobrecarga dos demais centros de distribuição e equilibrar a rede logística da companhia. A integração da cadeia de suprimentos deve contribuir para melhorar o atendimento a distribuidores, atacadistas e varejistas, com entregas mais ágeis e maior disponibilidade de produtos nos canais de compra. Localização estratégica amplia eficiência logística A escolha de Itupeva considera a proximidade com importantes unidades fabris e centros de distribuição da Unilever no interior de São Paulo. A localização permite otimizar rotas, reduzir deslocamentos e ampliar a eficiência da operação. Segundo Camiloti, a combinação entre tecnologia, integração operacional e planejamento logístico fortalece a competitividade da empresa, melhora o relacionamento com clientes e prepara a estrutura para sustentar o crescimento dos negócios no longo prazo. “Construímos uma operação mais conectada, inteligente e preparada para os desafios futuros. Hoje, contamos com uma estrutura que aumenta nos próximos anos nossa capacidade de resposta. Com essa integração, a Unilever tem a previsibilidade e a flexibilidade necessárias para crescer de forma segura, garantindo que nossos produtos cheguem às mãos dos consumidores com a excelência que a marca demanda” finaliza Camiloti. articles.title: 5 Leadership Lessons from Dave’s Hot Chicken CEO Jim Bitticks
articles.titleKo: 5 Leadership Lessons from Dave’s Hot Chicken CEO Jim Bitticks
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Jim Bitticks has been CEO of the brand since January. When Jim Bitticks joined Dave’s Hot Chicken as chief operating officer in July 2020, the brand had four locations. During a recent conversation on QSR Uncut , the now-CEO explained what the road to hundreds of units ( Dave’s opened a net of 120—the company’s most yet—last year to reach 358 ) has looked like. But his approach to growth wasn’t built around changing everything that came before him. Instead, Bitticks emphasizes understanding why a business works, protecting its defining qualities, and supporting the people who helped build it. Drawing on his experience at Dave’s, Blaze Pizza, and Carl’s Jr., here were five leadership lessons from the conversation. LISTEN TO THE FULL EPISODE HERE 1. Learn the business before imposing your playbook One of the questions Bitticks faced while starting at Dave’s was rather specific: Would he make the founders use tongs? It suggested someone had already tried to introduce an operational change without understanding what was working, and why. His response: ask how the founders operated, not immediately tell them how they should. The restaurants were generating strong sales. Bitticks had experience scaling brands, but he hadn’t created one. “I’ve never done what they’ve done at this point,” he said. Bitticks wasn’t arguing new leaders should withhold expertise. Rather, they should take time to understand before deciding where to guide. If a change was necessary, ask questions and explain the reasoning behind the motivation. That would be more productive than issuing a directive and leaving an existing team feeling like their prior work had been dismissed. The lesson: Bring your experience to a new role, but don’t mistake familiarity with another business for understanding this one. 2. Define what cannot be compromised—and teach it repeatedly Bitticks spoke to groups going through Dave’s brand training every week. There were three things he believed brought the company to this point: “mind-blowing” chicken, great service, and the brand’s distinctive vibe. Those principles provided a framework for decisions that otherwise could become mere calculations about speed or cost. If the choice was between offering subpar chicken faster and serving great chicken more slowly, Bitticks picked the latter. He credited Dave’s cofounder Arman Oganesyan with reinforcing the idea food worth returning for is also worth waiting for. The same thinking extended beyond the menu. The restaurants’ hand-painted art and music are part of the experience. They’re not incidental details you can strip away amid scale whenever a cheaper alternative appeared. For Bitticks, protecting those elements required more than mentioning them in a strategy meeting. The lesson: Identify the promises your brand makes to customers, then give employees clear guidance on how to protect them when competing priorities arise. 3. Build the support system before growth overwhelms it Bitticks came to Dave’s after helping Blaze Pizza expand from two locations to roughly 370. That experience taught him a distinction: Running restaurants and building the systems that allow other people to do so are different tasks. At Dave’s, he drew on relationships with former colleagues to establish that infrastructure. Early on, several members of the Blaze team worked part time to help get the new operation settled. Bitticks credits Juan Lopez, now Dave’s chief restaurant officer, and his team with preparing the systems needed to begin training and opening stores in about three months. But internal capabilities were only a part of it. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Eddie Merlot’s has introduced a limited-time holiday menu featuring premium steaks, seafood, and seasonal wine pairings, available November 3 through January 4 at all locations. The menu includes five featured entrées, including a 34-ounce Garlic Chili Tomahawk Ribeye, made with Certified Angus beef and marinated in fresh garlic chili oil. The dish is intended to serve two guests. Other selections include Surf & Turf, featuring a 6-ounce filet mignon and petite cold water lobster tail, and Pan-Roasted Salmon with a crispy lobster risotto cake, passion fruit butter sauce, and grilled asparagus. The holiday lineup also features Braised Short Rib served with heirloom carrots, fingerling potatoes, cipollini onions, and red wine demi-glace, as well as a pan-seared double-bone Elk Chop accompanied by sautéed fennel, cremini mushrooms, and red wine reduction. Wagyu Meatballs are available as an appetizer. The restaurant is also offering sommelier-selected wines, including Goldeneye Anderson Valley Pinot Noir, Duckhorn Napa Merlot, and Duckhorn Napa Cabernet Sauvignon. In addition to the seasonal menu, Eddie Merlot’s is introducing a holiday gift card promotion. From November 16 through January 3, customers who purchase $100 in gift cards online will receive $25 in bonus cards. The bonus cards can be redeemed during a future visit from January 4 through March 6, excluding February 12–14. As the holiday season approaches, Anthony’s Coal Fired Pizza & Wings is giving guests more reasons to celebrate. Throughout November, the restaurant brand is spreading holiday cheer with two in-restaurant merchandise giveaways featuring exclusive Anthony’s-branded bags, along with additional opportunities for guests to participate in the brand’s holiday celebrations. articles.title: Pura Vida Miami Expands in NYC
articles.titleKo: Pura Vida Miami Expands in NYC
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . PURA VIDA MIAMI, the lifestyle-driven wellness cafe brand known for its elevated all-day dining experience, announced the grand opening of its newest New York City location in Battery Park at 255 Vesey St. Located in Manhattan near Brookfield Place, the opening marks Pura Vida Miami’s continued expansion throughout New York City, bringing the brand’s presence to nine locations across the market and builds on the brand’s growing national footprint. The new Battery Park cafe follows several openings in key markets across the country, including most recently a flagship location in the Flatiron District this summer as Pura Vida Miami continues to introduce its signature blend of fresh food, thoughtful design and warm hospitality to new communities. To celebrate the brand-new Battery Park location, Pura Vida Miami will also feature the brand’s newly expanded frozen yogurt program, available exclusively at its Flatiron and Battery Park locations in New York City, offering a refreshing take on the brand’s signature better-for-you offerings. Guests can enjoy four signature creations for $12 each, including Berry Bliss (up to 12g of protein) and the new Strawberry Hazelnut (up to 11g of protein), featuring tart Greek frozen yogurt topped with chocolate hazelnut sauce, fresh strawberries, toasted coconut flakes, raw honey and sea salt; Pistachio Crunch (up to 21g), featuring pistachio butter, toasted mixed nuts, raw honey and sea salt; and Dubai Chocolate (up to 18g of protein), combining chocolate hazelnut sauce, pistachio butter, toasted nuts, coconut flakes, cacao nibs, raw honey and sea salt. For those looking to customize their experience, Pura Vida will also offer build-your-own frozen yogurt options for $12 with up to three toppings. The Battery Park cafe features indoor seating and outdoor seating and Pura Vida Miami’s signature airy, laid-back yet elevated finishes in white oak, Taj Mahal stone and greenery throughout. It also serves as a community third space, with homey, family-style seating at the back of the café. Pura Vida Miami’s full menu of fresh offerings will be available, including all-day breakfast, wraps, bowls, salads, sandwiches, high-protein plates, smoothies, coffee, matcha and seasonal specialties. “New York continues to be an incredibly important market for our brand and we’re excited to grow our presence in Battery Park,” said Omer Horev, Co-Founder and CEO of Pura Vida Miami. “It’s a dynamic neighborhood that brings together residents, professionals and visitors, and we see a natural alignment with the way our cafés are designed to fit into people’s everyday routine. We look forward to becoming part of the community and creating another welcoming space where guests can gather and enjoy the Pura Vida experience.” The Battery Park opening underscores Pura Vida Miami’s continued national expansion and growing presence in New York, with nine locations across New York and more than 50 locations nationwide with additional openings planned across the country. The Battery Park location will be open Monday-Saturday, 7:00AM-9:00PM, and Sunday, 7:00AM-8:00PM. The post Pura Vida Miami Expands in NYC appeared first on QSR Magazine .

Doom & Buster's runs November 16, 2026 through January 31, 2027 at Dave & Buster's locations nationwide. Dave & Buster’s is gone. In its place: Doom & Buster’s. As the world counts down to Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Doomsday , in theaters December 18, the ultimate destination for games, food and drinks has submitted. For a limited-time it surrenders its name, its stores, and its games to Doctor Doom, turning locations nationwide into the one place fans can step inside the world of Doomsday before it ever reaches the big screen. ALL SHALL PLAY. The submission begins this week. New Marvel-themed games and in-store experiences roll out today, building to the full Doom & Buster’s takeover on November 16: immersive Doomsday Zones, Collectible Power Cards, exclusive Marvel merchandise, themed prizes, a lineup of cocktails and mocktails, and DOOMHOUR, a surprise hour in which D&B Rewards members earn double tickets on green-swipe games. Resistance is pointless. PLAY IS MANDATORY. “When one of the biggest movies of the year is coming, you don’t put up a poster. You bend the knee,” said Jeremy Tucker, Chief Marketing Officer at Dave & Buster’s. “We gave Doom our name. We gave him the floor. We gave him the bar. Doom & Buster’s is a world fans can only walk into with us, and it’s built for the thing we do better than anyone: bringing people together to play, compete and be part of the action. All shall play. We’re just making it official.” “We’re always looking for brands who are willing to think bigger, and Dave & Buster’s did exactly that. Rather than creating a traditional promotion, they transformed their entire business into an immersive celebration of Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Doomsday, in theaters December 18. The result is a bold, fan-first experience that extends the story beyond the theater and into the real world in a way only Dave & Buster’s could,” said Lylle Breier, EVP, Partnerships, Promotions and Events, The Walt Disney Studios. Doom & Buster’s runs November 16, 2026 through January 31, 2027 at Dave & Buster’s locations nationwide. Games, attractions, and prizes vary by location. ALL SHALL PLAY. Enter the Doomsday Zone. The heart of the takeover is the Doomsday Zone, opening November 16 in stores nationwide. Themed entry arches mark the point of Doomsday domination. Beyond them, Marvel games, signage and game screens pull guests into the Doomsday Zone, where they can team up, race friends and hunt down themed prizes before and during the film’s run. Doom does not ask. Doom decrees. The first decrees take effect today, giving guests a head start on the action: MARVEL Cosmic Invasion : A fast-paced, 4-player, action beat’em up game. Choose two Super Heroes from across the Marvel Universe, switch between their abilities mid-fight, and hold the line against waves of enemies. Avengers: Roller Race & Battle: A 4-player head-to-head race with a villain to take down on the way. Fastest to the finish helps save the day. Human Crane: You are the claw. Strap in, lift off and get lowered into a sea of prizes, including brand-new inflatables. Mystery Crane: The classic claw with a twist. Every mystery pillow box hides a surprise. Thor’s Hammer Strike: Channel the god of thunder. One swing could top the leaderboard and score legendary ticket wins. The Arena: New games and a full immersive takeover bring a whole new world of play to life. Smash N Win: Take your shot and collect all 20 collectible character-themed balls before they’re gone. Avengers Themed Photo Booth: Snap a photo solo or with friends and family, then take home your photo as a keepsake from your visit. The takeover also brings a themed Avengers Funko pusher stocked with Avengers-only Funko prizes and limited-time Avengers-inspired cotton candy flavors. Flight Club, the world’s first Social Darts experience from global social entertainment operator State of Play Hospitality, officially opens on Wednesday, Nov. 11 at 31 Union Square West, bringing its tech-enabled take on the traditional game of darts to one of Manhattan’s most notable hospitality addresses. The concept’s highly anticipated New York debut marks Flight Club’s 13th U.S. location, with over 30 locations globally. Founded by Red Engine in London in 2015, Flight Club reimagined the classic pub pastime through proprietary technology, automated scoring and fast-paced multiplayer games. The New York venue brings Flight Club’s signature gameplay, craft cocktails and shareable bites to a 10,700-square-foot space within the historic 1902 Bank of the Metropolis building, which later became home to the iconic Blue Water Grill. Spanning two floors, the concept features 15 semi-private playing areas, known as oches, two bars, indoor and outdoor event spaces, with capacity for up to 300 guests. “Launching Flight Club New York has been many years in the making and marks a defining moment both for us as a company and Flight Club as a brand,” said Toby Harris, President and CEO of State of Play Hospitality, which operates Flight Club in North America under license. “As an iconic global city and a hub for best-in-class social entertainment, New York offers an incredible opportunity for us to introduce Social Darts® to new audiences and reimagine an entertainment venue of stunning quality. We’re thrilled to bring the energy of the city to life through Flight Club with a design that feels both unmistakably ours and uniquely New York.” DESIGN HERITAGE In designing the New York venue, Flight Club’s in-house design team sought to preserve many of the Bank of the Metropolis building’s original architectural details, including its marble floors, decorative cornicing, ornate ceilings and floral millwork, while layering in its signature Victorian fairground aesthetic. Warm wood finishes, antique furnishings, carousel-inspired details, layered florals, eclectic artwork and ambient lighting seamlessly blend the building’s historic character with Flight Club’s playful spirit. Upon arrival, guests are greeted by a vintage carousel horse, setting the tone for the Victorian-inspired design that unfolds throughout the space. The interiors also draw inspiration from New York itself, incorporating Hudson Valley landscapes, historic city scenes and subtle nods to Coney Island and Central Park. Playful Easter eggs include Yankees hats, hot dogs, apples and even a woman wearing the Statue of Liberty’s crown, while individual oches feature themes inspired by the city’s birdlife, literary figures and vintage fairgrounds. The main floor’s carousel bar serves as the heart of the venue, offering a lively gathering place and a destination for drinks and dining in its own right. Marquee lights respond to sound and music, echoing the movement of traditional fairground bulbs, while the patio and other flexible spaces extend Flight Club’s indoor-outdoor event offerings. Additional gameplay areas include the Cyclone Room featuring antique fairground panels and vintage Coney Island memorabilia; The Vault, which evokes the building’s rich history; and The Knickerbocker, an area reminiscent of New York’s golden age that can be utilized as a fully private events space with its own bar. The concept’s flexible layout is designed to allow guests to seamlessly move between playing, dining, drinking and socializing, with semi-private oches accommodating groups of up to 12. Lounge seating and bar areas create distinct environments suited to everything from intimate gatherings to large-scale events. articles.title: PJ’s Coffee Announces New Flavors for Holiday Season
articles.titleKo: PJ’s Coffee Announces New Flavors for Holiday Season
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The lineup draws inspiration from treats that make this time of year special. The season’s sweetest traditions arrive at PJ’s Coffee on Nov. 4, where two new creations — a sugar cookie-inspired latte and a sparkling pomegranate energy drink — meet the returning fan-favorite Peppermint Bark beverages for a limited time. From the aroma of fresh-from-the-oven cookies to the cool, chocolatey crunch of peppermint bark, the lineup draws inspiration from treats that make this time of year special: Santa’s Sugar Cookie Latte: Espresso and the flavor of warm sugar cookies blend with steamed milk, then get topped with whipped cream and a sprinkle of Sugar in the Raw for a sweet, crunchy finish. Snow-Capped Pomegranate Energy: A sparkling pomegranate-flavored energy drink topped with sweet cold foam for a bright, fruity pick-me-up. MTY Food Group operates dozens of concepts, including Cold Stone Creamery and Wetzel's Pretzels. Canada-based restaurant group Foodtastic publicly revealed that it proposed a roughly $704.2 million take over of fellow Canadian restaurant franchisor MTY Food Group. The two sides are now clashing over how negotiations have been handled. The disagreement escalated Wednesday when Foodtastic accused MTY of making misleading statements. The response came one day after MTY defended its decision to reject the proposal and announced a change in its chief executive position. Foodtastic first submitted its written proposal on October 15 and reiterated the offer on October 20. The company made its bid public Tuesday, arguing that MTY’s board had repeatedly declined to engage in substantive discussions. The proposed purchase price, $43 per share, represents a 32 percent premium to MTY’s October 30 closing share price and a 37 percent premium to its 30-day volume-weighted average price, according to Foodtastic. Foodtastic president and CEO Peter Mammas said the company sees significant opportunities in MTY’s restaurant portfolio, despite concerns regarding its recent performance. “I have long had tremendous respect for [MTY founder] Stanley Ma and the organization he built. MTY is a great company with excellent opportunities, but it has unfortunately not lived up to its full potential in recent years,” Mammas said in a statement. “We are very excited about the Proposed Transaction and believe it would not only deliver full and certain value to MTY’s shareholders, but also would be an incredible combination for its franchisees and employees.” Foodtastic operates approximately 1,200 restaurants across 30 brands, including Pita Pit, Freshii, Quesada, Second Cup, and Milestones. MTY is considerably larger, with 6,966 restaurants across more than 80 concepts in the U.S., Canada, and international markets. Its portfolio includes Cold Stone Creamery, Papa Murphy’s, Wetzel’s Pretzels, and Baja Fresh. Approximately 57 percent of MTY’s restaurants are in the U.S., 35 percent are in Canada, and 8 percent operate internationally. A combination would bring together two Canadian restaurant franchisors with extensive portfolios and experience acquiring established brands. However, the companies disagree over whether a sale represents the best outcome for MTY shareholders. MTY said Tuesday that its board unanimously rejected Foodtastic’s October proposals after reviewing them and determining that pursuing a transaction was not in the company’s or shareholders’ best interests. The company also disputed Foodtastic’s characterization of the negotiations, pointing to an extended strategic review that began in November 2025. MTY said its independent special committee considered a range of alternatives, including selling the entire company, divesting individual businesses, and continuing its existing strategy. During that process, Foodtastic received multiple extensions of an exclusivity period that MTY said were intended to allow the potential buyer to secure financing and complete a transaction. Following the review, MTY announced October 9 that it would pursue its own strategic plan instead of a sale. Foodtastic challenged that explanation Wednesday. “Foodtastic was not able to come to an agreement with MTY during the strategic review process, or subsequently, because [MTY] had unrealistic expectations about its value,” Foodtastic said in a statement. Foodtastic disputed MTY’s claim that it needed additional time to secure financing for the acquisition. For generations of customers and employees, Beef-A-Roo has represented more than a restaurant. From its roots in Rockford, Illinois, to the communities it has served across the Midwest and beyond, the brand has built a legacy defined by its people, distinctive menu, and loyal customer relationships. BAR II Op-Co is committed to preserving that legacy while establishing a stronger operational and financial foundation for its future. The company has secured restaurant locations across Illinois, Missouri, Indiana, Arkansas, and Kentucky, with additional opportunities in Michigan, Texas, and Kansas currently under negotiation. These efforts represent significant progress toward restoring restaurant operations, rebuilding relationships with landlords and vendors, and returning experienced restaurant teams to the communities they have served. Preserving Beef-A-Roo’s Rockford Roots Central to BAR II Op-Co’s rebuilding strategy is preserving Beef-A-Roo’s presence in Rockford, Illinois, where the brand’s history and community relationships run deepest. Through agreements with Bob Grottke and Alex Edwards of Corparoo, LLC, the company has made meaningful progress toward restoring operations in the Rockford market. These partnerships reflect a shared commitment to protecting the brand’s heritage, retaining experienced restaurant employees, and ensuring Beef-A-Roo remains part of the community where its story began. “From the moment we learned operations had ceased, my priority was to find a way to protect our employees’ livelihoods, preserve the brand, and create opportunities for experienced general managers to become restaurant owners,” said Jeremy Wise. “Working with Bob and Alex to preserve Beef-A-Roo’s presence in Rockford has been especially meaningful. Our Rockford employees represent decades of experience, dedication, and pride in this brand. They deserve an opportunity to return to something they helped build, and that commitment extends to our employees across every market we serve.” Under the leadership of Astolfo and Wise, BAR II Op-Co is working to establish dependable restaurant operations, strengthen vendor and landlord relationships, and develop a sustainable framework for long-term growth. The executive team is also working constructively with state, local, and federal agencies to address applicable outstanding matters and support regulatory compliance. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . KFC U.S.'s system sales declined 6 percent in Q3. KFC’s efforts to revive its U.S. business are producing encouraging results from individual menu launches, but the chicken chain is still struggling to translate that excitement into sustained sales growth. The brand’s domestic system sales declined 6 percent in the third quarter. The performance contrasted with KFC’s international operations, where new value platforms, menu innovation, and expansion are driving considerably stronger results. The domestic business continues to face intense competition from established chicken chains and newer fast-growing concepts. Yum! Brands CEO Chris Turner acknowledged the challenges during the company’s Q3 earnings, noting KFC U.S. is continuing to execute its turnaround strategy. The chain found some success during the period with the introduction of popcorn chicken, which attracted enough demand to sell out at numerous restaurants. The launch demonstrated KFC’s ability to generate customer interest through familiar products, even as its overall sales struggled. The company also faced a difficult comparison with Q3 2025, when a successful wings-and-wedges promotion contributed to sales performance. READ MORE : Taco Bell’s Recovery Gains Momentum After Challenging Cyclospora Issues Yum! is pursuing a comprehensive effort to modernize KFC, with initiatives spanning menu innovation, marketing, value, operations, and digital technology. The company wants KFC to become the world’s most modern chicken QSR brand. Its plans include a refreshed brand identity, a more consistent pipeline of limited-time offers, an everyday value platform, upgraded chicken tenders, additional sauces, and specialty beverages. Those initiatives are intended to give customers more reasons to visit and improve KFC’s competitiveness in a category where operators have invested aggressively in chicken sandwiches, tenders, and value meals. A major component of the strategy involves making KFC’s food more distinctive through new flavors and menu combinations. The company sees opportunities to improve its core chicken offerings and introduce products that appeal to different dining occasions. Beverages are becoming another priority, internationally at least. KFC’s new Kwench beverage platform has expanded to more than 1,000 restaurants across over 10 international markets, including six of the brand’s 20 largest markets. The program features specialty beverages such as sparkling lemonades, iced coffees, shakes, boba, and matcha, giving KFC an opportunity to attract customers who might not otherwise visit for a traditional chicken meal. Yum! expects Kwench to reach 2,000 restaurants by the end of 2026, with plans to double that footprint by the end of 2027. Expansion is continuing in Australia and Canada before the platform moves into additional major international markets. Kwench sales have more than doubled since the initial pilot, and approximately one in five KFC visits in Australia includes a Kwench beverage. The platform could eventually play a role in KFC’s domestic strategy, although Yum! has not announced a nationwide U.S. rollout. KFC is also investing in technology to improve service and reduce operational friction. Yum!’s Byte Kitchen display system is beginning to roll out across the U.S., providing employees with tools to manage kitchen demand and coordinate orders more efficiently. Early results from the limited number of participating restaurants have been promising. The company reported 8 percent faster drive-thru speeds, a 12 percent reduction in refunds, and a decrease of more than 20 seconds in delivery driver wait times. Overall, international markets excluding China reported 9 percent system sales growth during the third quarter. Same-store sales increased 4 percent, an improvement from the previous quarter.
