articles.title: QSR’s Best Brands to Work For in 2026
articles.titleKo: QSR’s Best Brands to Work For in 2026
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Five years into QSR’s Best Brands to Work For, the industry continues to prove that a great workplace can offer much more than a paycheck. Across this year’s class, restaurant jobs serve as starting points for careers that can stretch from the front line to the corporate office and even franchise ownership. Career growth is only one piece of the story. The brands featured in this fifth edition are putting resources into education, financial security, wellness, flexibility, recognition, and support outside the restaurant. Some provide tuition assistance and debt-free degrees. Others offer employee hardship funds, paid volunteer time, wellness stipends, predictable schedules, or routes to business ownership. Past Lists 2025 // 2024 // 2023 The 20 companies featured this year range from small to giant. Their programs and resources differ, but the goal is similar, and that’s to give employees a reason to see restaurant work as a place to build a career. That means creating opportunities to learn, advance, earn more, contribute ideas, and feel valued along the way. Chick-fil-A Unit Count: 3,500+ Chick-fil-A’s employment model is centered around locally owned restaurants, education, and internal mobility. Most restaurants are run by individual Owner-Operators who set compensation and benefits based on their local markets. Many offer health coverage, retirement benefits, meal discounts, and other perks. Restaurants also close every Sunday, continuing a tradition established by founder S. Truett Cathy. Education represents one of Chick-fil-A’s largest investments in restaurant employees. In 2026, the company awarded more than $29 million in Remarkable Futures Scholarships to more than 16,000 team members across the U.S., Canada, and Puerto Rico, its largest annual commitment in more than 50 years of scholarship giving. Since 1973, Chick-fil-A has invested more than $245 million in higher education for team members. Scholarships range from $1,500 to $25,000 and can be used for any area of study at accredited colleges, universities, or vocational-technical schools. There is no employment tenure requirement, and funds are paid up front. Recipients of $25,000 scholarships can also participate in a 12-month program featuring mentoring and professional development. Restaurant employment can also provide a route to business ownership. Over the past two years, 76 percent of newly selected Chick-fil-A Owner-Operators previously worked as Chick-fil-A team members. Most Owner-Operators oversee a single restaurant, allowing them to work closely with their teams and local communities. Team members also have access to Breadbox by Junior Achievement, which provides financial education covering budgeting, financial planning, and money skills. Restaurant employees can gain additional experience through mentorship and opportunities to develop skills in hospitality, teamwork, and service. Playa Bowls Unit Count: 407 Playa Bowls has made internal advancement a central part of its employee proposition as the concept has expanded beyond 400 locations. Over the past year, 53 percent of managers and leaders in its shops were promoted from within, along with 42 percent of managers and leaders on the Support Team. Those pathways can extend from entry-level restaurant positions into corporate roles. Aidan Rourke, for example, joined as a team member in 2020, advanced through shop leadership, supported new store openings, and was promoted to New Shop Openings Manager in August 2026. Director of Brand Marketing and Content Brenna Trumper has been with Playa Bowls even longer, having joined as the brand’s first team member in 2014. The company has also made progress with retention. articles.title: Economista de Plano Real acusa BC de causar rombo fiscal via juros
articles.titleKo: Economista de Plano Real acusa BC de causar rombo fiscal via juros
articles.originalSummary: O artigo de um dos economistas da equipe que elaborou o Plano Real, professor André Lara Resende, tem ganhado destaque nos últimos dias por acusar o Banco Central (BC) de causar desequilíbrio fiscal no Brasil por meio das altas taxas de juros. O especialista defende novas regras para as despesas e os juros no País. “Acuso o Banco Central de sustentar, em nome de uma teoria anacrônica, a taxa de juros que é a principal causa do desequilíbrio fiscal que diz combater.” Clique aqui e leia a íntegra do texto Eu Acuso: Uma Proposta para Eliminar os Juros Absurdos do ex-diretor do Banco Central e ex-presidente do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Social (BNDES). Formado pela PUC do Rio de Janeiro, André Lara Resende tem PhD em economia pelo Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), nos Estados Unidos, além de ter atuado em instituições financeiras no Brasil. O especialista questiona a teoria econômica defendida pelo mercado financeiro e pelo BC para justificar a taxa Selic em 13,75% ao ano. Segundo ranking da Moneyou , o Brasil tem a taxa de juros real mais alta do mundo. “Acuso a grande imprensa de repetir, sem exame, que o problema está no gasto primário, quando está nos juros. Acuso os analistas do mercado financeiro de confundir o interesse dos rentistas com a racionalidade econômica.” Escrito às vésperas do primeiro turno eleitoral, o artigo de André Lara Resende ainda acusou “todos os que, sabendo que juros absurdos inviabilizam o País, preferem o conforto do consenso ao incômodo da verdade”. O Banco Central justifica os juros elevados, entre outros motivos, devido às pressões inflacionárias e aos déficits fiscais primários nas contas públicas, que é quando as despesas superam as receitas, excluindo os gastos com a dívida. Segundo a autoridade monetária, os gastos primários maiores que arrecadação pressionam a inflação. Dívida e déficit públicos Apesar de reconhecer que o Brasil gasta mal e aloca recursos de forma “irracional”, como nos casos das emendas parlamentares, das vantagens salariais do Judiciário e das isenções tributárias “de toda ordem”, André Lara Resende demonstra que o Brasil tem um déficit fiscal pequeno, entre os menores do mundo. “Quando se exclui o serviço da dívida, as contas estão praticamente equilibradas. A grande despesa do Estado é com os juros sobre a dívida”, escreveu. A dívida pública brasileira cresceu de 71,7% do Produto Interno Bruto (PIB) em 2022 para cerca de 82,9% do PIB em agosto de 2026. Para combater esse aumento, analistas do mercado financeiro tem cobrado corte de despesas da União, o que tende a afetar as políticas sociais. O professor André Lara Resende reconhece que o crescimento da dívida é insustentável, mas destaca que o problema não está nos “gastos primários”, que são as despesas com serviços públicos que o mercado financeiro cobra para reduzir. “Nos últimos anos, exceto durante a Covid, o resultado primário foi apenas ligeiramente negativo; já o déficit nominal, puxado pelos juros, foi sempre alto e agora aproxima-se de 10% do PIB”, explicou. “O equilíbrio das contas públicas não é uma condição necessária e nem suficiente para o bom funcionamento da política econômica”, afirmou no artigo publicado no Substack. André Lara Resende concluiu que a redução da taxa de juros é a solução para o desequilíbrio fiscal no Brasil. Nos últimos 12 meses, os juros consumiram mais de R$ 1,1 trilhão do orçamento ou 8,9% do PIB. “A economia tem um problema básico: a extraordinariamente alta taxa básica de juros. Um problema que tem solução clara. Só é preciso vencer os preconceitos associados a uma teoria monetária e fiscal anacrônica”, concluiu. Juros e inflação O Banco Central sustenta que a atual taxa de juros é necessária para manter a inflação sob controle uma vez que a Selic elevada inibe o crescimento econômico e a demanda, forçando uma queda dos preços. articles.title: Bar92 Relaunches in NYC with New Menu and Cocktails from Michelin-Starred Chef
articles.titleKo: Bar92 Relaunches in NYC with New Menu and Cocktails from Michelin-Starred Chef
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Bar92, by Chef Sungchul Shim, is a clever play on words for the Korean pronunciation of 92, “구이” or in English, “gu-i.” Tucked beneath Michelin-selected Gui Steakhouse is casual cocktail lounge and jewel box space that offers a calm respite from the hustle and bustle of Times Square. This fall, Bar92 is relaunching through a revitalized cocktail program and an approachable new bar menu of American & French cuisine with Korean flair, upgrading Theatre District options for casual gatherings, pre- and post-theatre occasions, or a night out with friends. Hospitality and beverage consultant Sky Lim has reimagined Bar92’s cocktail program, translating Korean flavors and ingredients into classic cocktail forms. Inspired by the behaviors of the Theatre District—from a quick drink before the curtain rises to a nightcap after the final bow—the menu features familiar cocktails, each named after elements of the Broadway theaters just around the corner. Highlights include Standing Ovation, an Old Fashioned made with roasted corn silk tea, Woodford Reserve, and cold-pressed perilla oil; Opening Night, vodka-based with spicy-sweet Korean ginger, lime, and an ice-cold lager; and Red Curtain, pomegranate hongcho (a Korean fruit-flavored vinegar concentrate), jalapeño, and lime beneath a salted rim. The beverage menu also features non-proof cocktails as well as concise selection of curated wines and spirits. Inspired by American appetites, Bar92’s new menu brings a fresh perspective to beloved bar favorites through Chef Shim’s celebrated culinary vision, with each dish showcasing his Michelin-starred technique and creative approach. Broken down into Act I–raw bar, Act II–small plates, and Headliners, menu highlights include Gui Prime Rib Dip, 7oz of prime roast beef, caramelized onions, peppers, yuzu horseradish cream, and white American cheddar on a sesame seed hero roll with black garlic au jus; Prime Cheeseburger, house blend dry-aged prime beef, tomato, lettuce, and caramelized onion on brioche, with an option for a sunny side up egg or bacon; and thinly sliced, house-cured Duck Pastrami with fig jam, mustard seeds, and sourdough crostini. You may view the complete food & cocktail menu here. At the heart of the space, a custom mother of pearl tile backsplash depicts an ornate Korean landscape. Gold accents, a white marble countertop, and surrounding charcoal booths and high-top tables creates a lively front of bar area. Toward the back, a metal partition reveals a more intimate seating nook (available for private events), featuring a long banquette, brass details, and a low-hanging ribbed-wood ceiling modeled after a hanok, a traditional Korean house made from natural materials. Located on street level, Bar92 has a separate entrance immediately to the left of Gui’s main entrance. Editor’s Notes Chef Sungchul Shim is a multi-Michelin-starred chef and restaurateur based in New York City, celebrated for pioneering modern Korean fine dining. He holds degrees from The Culinary Institute of America (CIA) and refined his craft in some of the world’s most elite kitchens, including Thomas Keller’s Per Se (3★) and Eric Ripert’s Le Bernardin (3★). As the Executive Chef of Neta, he also earned a prestigious two-star review from The New York Times. As an entrepreneur, Chef Shim is the mastermind behind a powerhouse NYC hospitality portfolio, including the critically acclaimed, 1-Michelin-starred concepts Kochi and Mari, alongside Gui Steakhouse. Most recently, his global culinary influence was spotlighted on the international stage as a prominent contestant on Netflix’s global hit series, Culinary Class Wars: Season 2. The Salty operates more than 20 shops across eight states. Creative culinary brand The Salty Donut, known for its 24-hour brioche donuts, meticulously sourced coffee program and buzzy limited drops that create lines and move fast, has a new chief executive officer. To build upon the brand’s success, Maria Rivera, an accomplished hospitality executive with deep operational, brand expansion and capital markets experience, has been named The Salty’s new chief executive officer, reporting to The Salty’s board of directors. Rivera joined in the spring and has spent the past four months inside the business, bringing operational discipline to every part of the company and setting the leadership structure for its next phase. Her focus is simple: Make every shop as good as the first, own the morning and build what comes next. Rivera has spent her career building brands people love and the companies behind them. As President of Krispy Kreme U.S., she led the brand during a period when it ranked number one in brand love. Later, as CEO of Smalls Sliders, she built a 320-unit committed development pipeline. She has also served as CEO of Starbird, Director of Operations at Hilton and Walt Disney Company, Regional VP at Darden Restaurants and TGI Fridays, and is the Founder and Managing Partner of RC Hospitality Group, an operator-led venture studio that builds and scales emerging brands with purpose. The Salty operates more than 20 shops across eight states. Amanda Pizarro founded The Salty while still in college alongside her then-boyfriend, now-husband Andy Rodriguez as a pop-up shop. Under the new structure, Pizarro becomes founder and chief brand officer and Rodriguez continues as co-founder and board member. “We’ve watched Maria work from the inside since spring,” said Pete Pizarro, chairman of the board. “Her deep experience and clear love for the brand made the decision easy.” “As the first Latina to lead a U.S. restaurant brand, I couldn’t be more excited to join one that is Latina founded,” Rivera said. “The Salty already has the hardest thing to build: guests who line up for it. My job is everything behind that line; the systems, the team and the discipline that make every shop as good as the first. What comes next? People will have to see for themselves.” “We built something people love,” Pizarro said. “I’m excited to work alongside Maria, who has been such an evangelist for The Salty, to help continue to build the company to take it everywhere it belongs while preserving what makes it special.” The Salty is known for its creative collaborations with brands like Poppi, Snif, Summer Fridays, Salt & Straw, Natalie’s Juices, Mini Cooper and more, as well as its intentional commitment to its local communities through partnerships and events. More exciting partnerships will be announced soon. For more information, visit saltydonut.com. The post The Salty Donut Names Maria Rivera CEO appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Sekron Digital lança bag antifurto reutilizável para farmácias
articles.titleKo: Sekron Digital lança bag antifurto reutilizável para farmácias
articles.originalSummary: A Sekron Digital lançou uma bag antifurto reutilizável para farmácias e drogarias. A bolsa conta com sensor integrado e foi desenvolvida para proteger produtos pequenos, embalagens irregulares e itens que não podem receber etiquetas eletrônicas convencionais, como medicamentos termolábeis, dermocosméticos, suplementos e fórmulas infantis. O dispositivo permanece fechado durante a compra e é aberto no caixa com um desacoplador, após o registro dos produtos. Caso atravesse as antenas antifurto sem a liberação, o sistema aciona o alarme da loja. “A bag foi pensada para proteger produtos que muitas vezes são difíceis de etiquetar ou que exigem proteção especial por conta de seus altos valores. Ela reúne proteção e praticidade em uma solução reutilizável, sem exigir que a equipe aplique e remova etiquetas item por item”, afirma Rafael Bernardini, CEO da Sekron Digital. A bag funciona com sistemas acústico-magnéticos (AM) já instalados nos estabelecimentos. Dessa forma, farmácias que contam com antenas compatíveis podem utilizar a solução sem substituir os equipamentos ou realizar obras. Para lojas que ainda não possuem o sistema, a Sekron Digital oferece antenas, bolsas, instalação e suporte técnico. Feita de material transparente, a bolsa permite que a equipe visualize os produtos sem abri-la. O fechamento até o caixa também dificulta a troca de embalagens e a ocultação de itens. Prevenção de perdas no varejo farmacêutico Por ser reutilizável, a bag dispensa a etiquetagem individual dos produtos e pode reduzir o uso de etiquetas descartáveis. O dispositivo também evita que adesivos cubram informações das embalagens, como validade, lote e registro na Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa). Segundo a 9ª Pesquisa de Perdas no Varejo Brasileiro, elaborada pela Associação Brasileira de Prevenção de Perdas ( Abrappe ), o índice de perdas do varejo farmacêutico ficou em aproximadamente 1,24% do faturamento em 2025, com impacto estimado em R$ 2,99 bilhões. As perdas não identificadas, que incluem principalmente furtos, roubos e divergências de estoque sem causa esclarecida, passaram de 0,43% para 0,49% da receita no período, uma alta de cerca de 12%. articles.title: Golden Corral to Host ‘Thank You’ Buffet and Breakfast on Veterans Day to Thank All Military Personnel
articles.titleKo: Golden Corral to Host ‘Thank You’ Buffet and Breakfast on Veterans Day to Thank All Military Personnel
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Golden Corral will once again salute current U.S. service members, retired military, and veterans by inviting them to enjoy a FREE “Thank You” buffet and beverage at restaurants nationwide on Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov. 11, from 4 p.m. to close for its 26th Annual Military Appreciation Night (MAN). In partnership with DAV (Disabled American Veterans), Golden Corral will raise funds for local DAV chapters, with representatives stationed at participating restaurants for several weeks. Guests can support DAV by rounding up their checks at the register or by making a donation directly to their local DAV chapter. All funds raised will support DAV’s mission of providing no-cost services to veterans, their families, caregivers, and survivors. For the first time, the fundraising effort will continue through Sunday, Nov. 29, providing additional opportunities to support DAV beyond Veterans Day. This year, also for the first time, Golden Corral will partner with retired U.S. Navy SEAL and veterans advocate Marcus Luttrell to promote Military Appreciation Night. “Marcus Luttrell is both a Navy Cross and Purple Heart recipient, and knows better than most how much the U.S. Military and their families sacrifice to keep America free. Golden Corral is honored to join with Marcus to raise more awareness for this important annual event,” said Skip Hanke, 4th-generation U.S. Navy veteran and Chief Marketing Officer at Golden Corral Corporation. “Military Appreciation Night is one of the most meaningful traditions we have at Golden Corral, and each year we’re reminded of how much this night means to the veterans and active-duty military we welcome into our restaurants,” said Lance Trenary, CEO of Golden Corral. “For 26 years, our guests and team members have come together to say thank you in a way that goes far beyond a meal. It’s our way of showing our appreciation and gratitude, and we’re excited to partner with Marcus Luttrell to build on that tradition, support the incredible work of DAV, and most importantly honor the men and women who have sacrificed so much for our country.” In 2025, Golden Corral restaurants served nearly 180,000 complimentary “Thank You” meals and raised nearly $1 million for DAV chapters. Since 2001, Golden Corral’s Military Appreciation Night has served nearly 6.9 million free meals and raised more than $21.5 million for local DAV chapters. Golden Corral’s Military Appreciation Night offer includes a free buffet and beverage and is available for dine-in only to current U.S. service members, retired military, and veterans. No military identification is required, and the meal does not extend to spouses, friends, or other family members. The complimentary “Thank You” meal gives guests access to Golden Corral’s legendary endless buffet, featuring more than 150 items, including USDA grilled-to-order steaks, fried chicken, pot roast, meatloaf, mac and cheese, fresh salads, sides, desserts and the brand’s famous yeast rolls. With scratch-made, comforting favorites and new dishes regularly joining the lineup, guests have plenty to enjoy as they gather around the table this Veterans Day. Throughout the year, Golden Corral builds on its tradition with additional initiatives that make a difference beyond the annual MAN event. Its support of Camp Corral helps provide children of wounded, ill, and fallen service members with summer camp experiences at no cost to their families. Through traditional camp activities and specialized programming, Camp Corral provides opportunities for children to build peer connections, strengthen self-confidence, and develop coping skills while spending time with others who understand the unique challenges of growing up in a military family. Since 2011, Golden Corral and DAV have raised more than $21 million for Camp Corral, with over $2 million raised in 2026 alone. Golden Corral

One beloved Orlando restaurant is passing the torch to another rising culinary concept in the College Park neighborhood. Pacchioni’s, the popular food truck known for taking the classic Philadelphia cheesesteak on a flavorful trip around the world, is preparing to open its first brick-and-mortar location in the former Pizza Bruno space at 2429 Edgewater Drive, Orlando, FL 32804. Set to open in early December, the new restaurant, Pacchioni’s Cheesesteaks & Pizza, will bring its signature globally inspired cheesesteaks and an inventive new pizza menu to the heart of College Park. The approximately 1,500-square-foot restaurant marks an exciting milestone for Pacchioni’s, which launched its food truck in February 2025 and has been making a name for itself with its creative approach to the iconic Philly cheesesteak. Founded by Daniel Pacchioni, the concept combines familiar comfort food with bold international flavors, offering a culinary adventure inspired by destinations around the world. While Pacchioni’s signature cheesesteaks will remain at the heart of the menu, the new restaurant will introduce an entirely new lineup of inventive pizzas, giving the former Pizza Bruno space a fresh new chapter while maintaining its connection to Orlando’s vibrant restaurant scene. “Opening our first brick-and-mortar restaurant is a dream come true, and doing it in College Park makes it even more special,” says Pacchioni. “We lived just two streets away for five years, so this really feels like coming home. The response to our food truck has been incredible, and we’re excited to build on that momentum and take our ideas even further. For us, this is about more than opening a restaurant. It’s about creating something meaningful with longtime friends, becoming part of a neighborhood we already love and giving Orlando food lovers something new and unexpected. We’re especially honored to have Bruno’s blessing and thankful for all his support and mentorship and who knows, maybe there’s a few surprise collaborations in the near future. We can’t wait to share this next chapter with the community.” Pacchioni is joined in the new venture by his longtime friends and new business partners Yeosh Bendayan and Jon Ruhff, who bring their entrepreneurial experience to the restaurant industry. Together, Bendayan and Ruhff have built and operated successful businesses, including Push Button Creative Audio, specializing in audio branding, and Southeast Chevy Parts, serving the classic Chevrolet restoration community. Their experience spans business development, marketing, brand building, customer experience and day-to-day operations. Now, they’re applying that collective expertise to an exciting new chapter in the restaurant business, working alongside their new partner to create a distinctive dining experience in College Park. “Pizza Bruno has been such a special part of College Park, and when it came time to pass the torch, I wanted to make sure the space was in the right hands,” says Owner Bruno Zacchini. “Daniel, Yeosh, Jon and team were a natural choice. I love the team’s passion, creativity and vision for what they want to bring to the neighborhood. They share the same entrepreneurial spirit and commitment to great food, and I’m especially excited to share my input on their new restaurant. I can’t wait to see what they create in this next chapter.” Pacchioni’s existing menu, developed in collaboration with Michelin-starred chef Mike Collantes, takes guests on a culinary journey with globally inspired cheesesteaks featuring premium ingredients and unexpected flavor combinations. articles.title: Smalls Sliders Signs 3-Unit Deal in Northwest Indiana
articles.titleKo: Smalls Sliders Signs 3-Unit Deal in Northwest Indiana
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Smalls Sliders , the industry-disrupting cheeseburger slider brand, has signed a new three-Can development agreement with Keystone Management Group to bring the rapidly growing concept to Northwest Indiana. The agreement marks Keystone Management Group’s second development deal with Smalls Sliders, building on the five-Can agreement the group signed for Louisville, Kentucky, in late 2025. With its latest commitment, Keystone Management Group now plans to develop eight Smalls Sliders Cans across the two markets. Backed by more than 20 years of restaurant operations and franchise ownership experience, the group saw an opportunity to deepen its investment in Smalls Sliders after experiencing firsthand the brand’s differentiated model and growth potential. “After signing our first agreement with Smalls Sliders, we became even more confident in the opportunity behind the brand and knew we wanted to continue growing alongside the team,” said a spokesperson with Keystone Management Group.“Northwest Indiana is a natural next step for us, and we’re excited to introduce Smalls Sliders to new communities while continuing to build out our portfolio with a concept we believe has tremendous potential.” The team plans to develop three Cans throughout the region,building on Smalls Sliders’ growing presence in Indiana following the opening of the brand’s first Can in the state in Muncie earlier this September. The new development will introduce Smalls Sliders’ signature cheeseburger sliders, waffle fries and shakes to more guests while further establishing the brand’s footprint across Indiana. “Having an experienced group choose to expand its commitment to Smalls Sliders speaks volumes about both the strength of our model and the relationships we’re building with our operators,” said Ryan Crumley, Chief Development Officer at Smalls Sliders. “Keystone Management Group brings deep operational experience and an understanding of what it takes to grow restaurant concepts across multiple markets. We’re thrilled to continue our relationship with the team as they bring three Cans to Northwest Indiana.” Smalls Sliders serves fresh, cooked-to-order cheeseburger sliders, seasoned waffle fries, and hand-spun milkshakes from its signature Smorange™-colored shipping containers, called “Cans.” This deliberately simple menu, focused on quality and speed, has propelled the brand from its first location in 2019 to over 55 Cans now open and hundreds in development across 30 states. As part of its continued expansion in the region, Smalls Sliders is actively seeking real estate opportunities throughout the market. The brand is currently evaluating sites for future Cans and encourages those interested in connecting with the team to contact realestate@smallssliders.com and Stephen Smith at stephen.smith@smallssliders.com . For more information on Smalls Sliders, slide thru to www.smallssliders.com or visit www.smallsslidersfranchising.com to learn more about franchising opportunities. Wetzel’s Pretzels, the iconic brand known for its fresh, hand-rolled pretzels, is expanding its presence in South Carolina with a new bakery inside the Walmart Supercenter at 605 Saint James Ave. The Goose Creek bakery will be operated by Mathieu and Hannah Rajaonah. The husband-and-wife duo relocated to the Charleston area in 2025 and saw an opportunity to bring the brand to South Carolina. They opened their first location with the brand earlier this year in Summerville, marking the brand’s first brick-and-mortar location in South Carolina. They look to continue to grow with Wetzel’s in the South Carolina region. “We’re eager to open our second location with Wetzel’s Pretzels in just under one year as we expand the brand in South Carolina,” said Mathieu Rajaonah. “The partnership with Walmart has allowed us to connect with the community, and we look forward to introducing the brand to guests in Goose Creek.” The new location builds on Wetzel’s Pretzels growing partnership with Walmart, bringing the brand’s freshly baked pretzels and refreshing drinks to shoppers in a convenient retail setting. Guests can enjoy a quick snack while shopping for everyday essentials. “We’re thrilled to continue growing Wetzel’s Pretzels in South Carolina and have Mathieu and Hannah leading the way to handheld happiness in Goose Creek,” said Eric Weigel, Brand Leader at Wetzel’s Pretzels. “As we continue to develop into new markets and share our iconic flavors with the local community. We’re confident the Goose Creek bakery will be a hit with shoppers looking for a fresh, fast, and fun snack experience.” Wetzel’s Pretzels continues to grow through nontraditional retail locations, including Walmart stores, allowing the brand to reach new customers and bring its signature pretzels and snacks to more communities. articles.title: Região Norte lidera interesse por delivery de farmácia no Google, revela iFood
articles.titleKo: Região Norte lidera interesse por delivery de farmácia no Google, revela iFood
articles.originalSummary: A Região Norte concentra quatro dos dez Estados com maior volume de buscas pelo termo “delivery de farmácia” no Google Brasil, com o Amapá na liderança entre setembro de 2025 e agosto de 2026, segundo levantamento do iFood. Na sequência aparecem Roraima, Rondônia e Acre, também da Região Norte, seguidos por Sergipe, Piauí e Alagoas, no Nordeste. O Distrito Federal e Mato Grosso do Sul, no Centro-Oeste, e São Paulo, no Sudeste, completam o ranking. O levantamento considerou o volume de buscas no Google, proporcional a cada 100 mil habitantes, e identificou os Estados com maior interesse pela modalidade. Os dados não representam, necessariamente, intenções de compra ou comportamentos dos consumidores fora do ambiente digital. Farmácia avança na oferta de entregas digitais A integração das farmácias aos canais digitais permite que os consumidores consultem catálogos, comparem preços e comprem medicamentos e produtos de higiene sem precisar ir até uma loja. A entrega depende da disponibilidade do estabelecimento e das modalidades oferecidas. O prazo de entrega varia conforme a localização, a disponibilidade de estoque e as condições logísticas de cada operação. Dados divulgados pela Associação Brasileira de Redes de Farmácias e Drogarias ( Abrafarma ), em março de 2026, mostram que os pedidos feitos a distância nas 29 redes associadas cresceram 57,7% em 2025, movimentando R$ 22,6 bilhões. Segundo a entidade, cerca de duas em cada dez vendas dessas redes foram realizadas por canais de entrega. A expansão do serviço depende de fatores como cobertura das entregas, organização dos estoques, conservação dos produtos e cumprimento das normas sanitárias. No caso dos medicamentos, o transporte precisa preservar as condições indicadas para cada produto, incluindo eventuais exigências de temperatura e umidade. Embora as plataformas digitais conectem consumidores e farmácias, a entrega de medicamentos exige cuidados específicos, diferentes dos aplicados ao transporte de outras mercadorias. All Active Duty Military, Veterans, Reserves, and National Guard members who dine in at participating Applebee’s restaurants will receive a complimentary full-size entrée from an exclusive Veterans Day menu as a heartfelt thank-you for their service.* This year marks the 19 th consecutive year Applebee’s has honored service members and veterans with complimentary meals on Veterans Day. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The KFC Foundation, a nonprofit that supports KFC restaurant employees and their communities, announces the launch of the Education Assistance Program in collaboration with InStride, a leading workforce development company. The program supports KFC team members in earning degrees, building new skills, and gaining professional credentials. Through the partnership, eligible KFC U.S. restaurant employees* can now access $5,000 each school year in education assistance to use toward a variety of online learning options. The program provides personalized recommendations to help participants find degree and certification pathways that match their goals, interests, and experience. “This partnership reflects the KFC Foundation’s continued commitment to investing in KFC restaurant employees’ futures and making education more accessible,” said KFC Foundation Executive Director Emma Horn. “By providing flexible online learning opportunities, we’re helping employees build new skills, reach their goals, and take the next step in their personal and professional development.” All team members who enroll in the Education Assistance Program can access the education assistance to use toward their choice of over 1,000 degrees, industry and professional certifications, trade programs, and short skill-building courses. Participating employees can access educational services through InStride’s academic network of more than 2,500 programs from leading public universities and education providers, including Arizona State University, ed2go Career Training, Franklin University, Indiana Tech, and more. “Career growth looks different for everyone. We’re proud to partner with the KFC Foundation to connect KFC restaurant employees with a wide range of learning opportunities, from degrees and professional certifications to skills-based training, so employees can choose what fits their goals,” said Craig Maloney, CEO of InStride. In addition to the $5,000 coverage, the Education Assistance Program offers up to $600 for course books and $100 for course fees annually to support employees in furthering their education and enhancing their skills. Team members who have already completed some college courses may be able to transfer their credits at select institutions and keep moving forward within the program. Since 2012, the KFC Foundation has awarded over $40 million in scholarships and tuition assistance to more than 11,000 KFC restaurant employees. articles.title: Paris Baguette Saw Growth Momentum Continue in Third Quarter

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Paris Baguette, a top-ranked global bakery café franchise and the No. 1 bakery café in Entrepreneur’s Franchise 500 for six consecutive years, continued to grow across North America in the third quarter of 2026. The brand signed new franchise agreements, secured leases for future locations, and opened new locations while continuing to see steady guest demand. Earlier this year, Paris Baguette celebrated six consecutive years of positive comparable sales and traffic growth. That momentum continued through Q3, with the brand awarding 32 franchise agreements, signing 22 leases and opening 15 bakery cafés during the quarter. Year to date, Paris Baguette has awarded 119 franchise agreements, signed 83 leases and opened 53 new locations. Third-quarter highlights included an agreement for the first Paris Baguette café in Maine, as well as agreements with existing Texas franchisees to develop six locations in Missouri and three in Pennsylvania. The brand also opened its first New Mexico café in Albuquerque, expanding its presence into another new market. With 341 open locations and 40 additional locations planned to open by the end of the year, Paris Baguette is fast approaching 400 cafes and $1B in systemwide sales. That momentum was further recognized in early October, when the brand ranked No. 41 on the Franchise Times Top 400 , a ranking of the largest franchise systems in the U.S. by global systemwide sales. “Paris Baguette was built around a simple idea: the neighborhood bakery café should be a place where people come together,” said CEO Darren Tipton . “As we continue growing across North America, we’re seeing that idea resonate with franchisees and guests alike. We’re incredibly excited to bring the warmth, hospitality and everyday joy of Paris Baguette to even more neighborhoods.” In addition to meaningful franchise growth in the third quarter, Paris Baguette also continued to expand its presence beyond its café footprint. The brand launched a national partnership with Dancing with the Stars for Season 35, featuring limited-time Mirrorball beverages, National Dance Day promotions and a sweepstakes giving fans the opportunity to attend the Season 35 Los Angeles finale. The brand also continued to strengthen its position within the franchise and real estate industries, with its executive team participating in International Council of Shopping Centers (ICSC) events and the International Franchise Expo (IFE) in Toronto. Sage Kriss , director of real estate, was a featured speaker at ICSC Columbus. “We’re building more than a network of cafés, we’re building places where people can gather, connect and feel at home,” Tipton said. “That’s at the heart of Paris Baguette, and it’s incredibly rewarding to see our franchisees share that vision as we move closer to 1,000 cafés across North America.” With 40 additional cafés planned to open in Q4, Paris Baguette is carrying that momentum into the final quarter of the year. As the brand expands its footprint, more communities will be able to enjoy its handcrafted cakes, pastries and breads baked fresh daily, along with sandwiches, salads, and made-to-order beverages. New and returning menu items are available at participating Long John Silver's locations nationwide. Cold weather, warm chowder, and a few familiar favorites. Starting Nov. 2, Long John Silver’s is serving up comfort with the return of its creamy Clam Chowder. And there’s plenty more to cozy up with, including the $6 Fish Basket, creamy Mac and Cheese and a few sweet treats to round out the season. “There’s just something about a warm bowl of Clam Chowder when the weather turns cold. Available in small or large sizes, it’s just as satisfying on its own as it is alongside a meal. And for those who want a little bit of everything, the new Fish and Chowder Platter pairs two pieces of hand-battered fish, Clam Strips, a small Clam Chowder, one side, two hushpuppies, and Crumblies. To close out a year of $6 Baskets, the brand is bringing its signature hand-battered fish back into the spotlight. When it comes to the holiday dessert table, choosing just one treat is nearly impossible. That’s why Baskin-Robbins is giving guests a little bit of everything this season with its new Dessert Table Collection, a lineup inspired by the familiar flavors of holiday favorites like pumpkin pie, spice cake and frosted sugar cookies. Plus, the fan-favorite Baskin-Robbins Turkey Cake is back to bring a sweet surprise to Thanksgiving celebrations. Inspired by the experience of piling your plate with a little bit of every holiday dessert, the Dessert Table Collection brings together cozy, nostalgic flavors across two new ice creams, a sundae and a shake: • Triple Treat Feast Ice Cream: Why settle between spice cake, pumpkin pie or pecan pie when this sweet treat delivers all three flavors in one. articles.title: Inadimplência atinge recorde de 84,2 milhões de brasileiros
articles.titleKo: Inadimplência atinge recorde de 84,2 milhões de brasileiros
articles.originalSummary: A inadimplência no Brasil atingiu um recorde de 84,2 milhões de pessoas em setembro, segundo o Mapa da Inadimplência e Renegociação de Dívidas, divulgado pela Serasa. O número representa um aumento em relação a agosto, quando 83,9 milhões de brasileiros estavam negativados. O volume total de débitos acumulados chegou a R$ 597,4 bilhões, alta de 0,90% na comparação mensal. A dívida média por inadimplente ficou em R$ 7.093,83. Pela primeira vez no levantamento, as financeiras assumiram a segunda posição entre os principais credores, concentrando 20,66% das dívidas. O segmento ultrapassou as contas básicas de água, luz e gás, que representam 20,32% dos débitos. Os bancos e cartões de crédito seguem na liderança, com 27,16% das pendências. As mulheres representam 50,5% dos brasileiros negativados, enquanto os homens correspondem a 49,5%. A faixa etária de 41 a 60 anos concentra a maior parcela dos inadimplentes, com 35,7% do total. Na sequência estão pessoas de 26 a 40 anos (33,2%), consumidores acima de 60 anos (20,1%) e jovens de 18 a 25 anos (11%). articles.title: Abrasel vê ‘notícia ruim’ em CBS de 11,3% para alimentação e alerta para alta de custos
articles.titleKo: Abrasel vê ‘notícia ruim’ em CBS de 11,3% para alimentação e alerta para alta de custos
articles.originalSummary: O presidente do Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU), Vital do Rêgo Filho, informou nesta quarta-feira, 28, que a alíquota de referência da Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS) foi calculada em 11,3%. A nova alíquota, que começa a valer em janeiro de 2027, preocupa a Associação Brasileira de Bares e Restaurantes ( Abrasel ), por superar a estimativa anterior de 9,21%. Para a Abrasel, a nova alíquota é uma notícia ruim, especialmente para os estabelecimentos de alimentação fora do lar. A entidade afirma que o percentual se soma ao aumento de custos já previsto pelo setor com a proibição da escala 6×1 . O número também pode pesar na conta final da reforma. Somada aos 18,70% projetados pelo Comitê Gestor para o IBS, a CBS de 11,35% pode levar a alíquota-padrão a cerca de 30%, acima dos 26,5% estabelecidos como referência pela Lei Complementar 214/2025. “O empresário do setor já está refazendo as contas para enfrentar o fim da 6×1. Agora descobre que o novo imposto federal vai começar em patamar elevado. Essa conta chega ao consumidor, com preços mais altos, e ao trabalhador, com menos vagas”, afirma Paulo Solmucci, presidente da Abrasel. A Abrasel reconhece que o IBS será cobrado à alíquota de 0,1% em 2027 e que a projeção de 18,70% ainda pode ser revista. Mesmo assim, a entidade avalia que a decisão evidencia o custo da ampliação dos gastos pelo governo. A associação também destaca o cenário de preocupação com o aumento de custos, os juros elevados e a necessidade de ajuste fiscal. Na avaliação da Abrasel, o cálculo, baseado na metodologia da Receita Federal, sinaliza uma preferência do governo pelo aumento da arrecadação em vez do corte de gastos. O setor tem direito a uma redução de 40% nas alíquotas, garantida pelo regime específico da reforma tributária. O desconto, porém, incide sobre a alíquota de referência, o que significa que, quanto maior o percentual definido, maior será o imposto pago por bares e restaurantes. A Abrasel alerta ainda para um choque de custos previsto para dezembro, que pode empurrar a economia para a recessão. O Senado tem até 15 de dezembro para fixar a alíquota de referência da CBS. Caso não vote dentro do prazo, valerá o percentual calculado pelo TCU. articles.title: Phillips 66 and Restaurant Technologies are Converting Used Cooking Oil into Sustainable Aviation Fuel
articles.titleKo: Phillips 66 and Restaurant Technologies are Converting Used Cooking Oil into Sustainable Aviation Fuel
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) starts in a place most people never expect: the deep fryer. Phillips 66 and Restaurant Technologies, Inc. (RTI) have a long-term agreement to supply used cooking oil from U.S. restaurants to produce renewable fuels in California, strengthening supply for lower carbon fuel markets. RTI supplies Phillips 66 with high quality, traceable, ISCC certified used cooking oil (UCO) to support renewable diesel and SAF production at the Phillips 66 Rodeo Renewable Energy Complex in California, one of the largest renewable fuels facilities in the world. The ISCC certification aligns with the United Nations Global Compact and recognizes that the company meets the highest standards for renewable feedstocks, greenhouse-gas reductions, and circular economy practices. “This strategic agreement delivers feedstock optionality and reliable, domestic supply to support renewable fuels production at our Rodeo Renewable Energy Complex,” said Mark Hughes, Senior Vice President, Commercial, Phillips 66. “It underscores the strength of our Commercial organization and our ability to actively connect domestic supply with operations and customers for a more robust integrated value chain.” RTI operates a closed loop automated cooking oil management solution that keeps used cooking oil clean, separated, and largely free from excess water, food waste, and other contaminants at the source. Compared with more traditional open collection systems, this approach produces a more consistent and higher quality feedstock that requires less pretreatment and increases the amount of usable fuel that can be produced. “Quality starts in the kitchen,” said Ronald Cardwell, Director of Commodity Strategy at RTI. “Our system keeps impurities out, so more of every gallon we collect can be transformed into renewable fuel, which improves efficiency from collection to production.” Once RTI collects used cooking oil from its network of more than 45,000 restaurants, hotels, casinos, colleges and other food service operations across 41 markets nationwide, the UCO, along with other waste-based feedstocks, is converted into renewable fuels at Phillips 66’s Rodeo Renewable Energy Complex. The UCO is first cleaned, then heated and combined with hydrogen to produce neat unblended SAF. The hydrogen and carbon atoms of the oil are rearranged into SAF hydrocarbons, which are blended and certified as renewable jet fuel meeting ASTM standards. SAF can reduce lifecycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by up to 80% compared with conventional jet fuel. Those reductions can be measured, certified, and used for emissions reporting by customers. Once SAF is produced, the Phillips 66 Aviation team sells it to customers to help meet their decarbonization commitments. “SAF is an investment in energy security because it diversifies aviation fuel supply options,” said Hughes. “The world needs all forms of energy, and Phillips 66 is uniquely positioned to provide both conventional and renewable fuels, which are supported by securing reliable feedstocks.” Feedstocks create value by turning waste streams and renewable byproducts into useful energy inputs, supporting a broader feedstock ecosystem. By combining large scale renewable fuels production capability with a reliable supply of high-quality feedstock, this agreement highlights how everyday restaurant operations can help advance a lower-carbon energy system. “Airlines and corporate customers need solutions they can use now, to support supply needs and decarbonization commitments,” Cardwell added. “This agreement demonstrates that the pieces are in place to scale high-quality feedstocks and renewable fuels production capability to make lower carbon flight more available and more achievable.” The post Phillips 66 and Restaurant Technologies are Converting Used Cooking Oil into Sustainable Aviation Fuel app

articles.title: A revolução invisível da longevidade: 4 mercados que vão crescer com as mudanças demográficas
articles.titleKo: A revolução invisível da longevidade: 4 mercados que vão crescer com as mudanças demográficas
articles.originalSummary: Vivemos uma transformação sem precedentes na história humana. Três forças estruturais estão redesenhando o comportamento e o consumo global: O aumento expressivo da expectativa de vida , cria uma fase pós-carreira ativa de 20 a 40 anos. Famílias cada vez menores e dispersas , reduz a rede de apoio tradicional doméstica. O duplo desafio do tédio e da solidão , que desponta como uma das maiores dores de saúde pública e bem-estar do século 21. Nesse cruzamento, a chamada economia prateada deixa de ser um nicho restrito aos cuidados médicos para se consolidar como um motor de negócios voltados à autonomia, conexão humana, lazer e vitalidade. “Filhos de aluguel”: autonomia cotidiana e pequenos reparos Com filhos morando em outras cidades, rotinas corporativas sufocantes e menos herdeiros por família, tarefas operacionais simples tornam-se problemas difíceis de resolver: trocar uma lâmpada em pé-direito alto, configurar a smart TV, instalar uma fechadura eletrônica ou consertar um vazamento na torneira. O modelo de negócio: serviços de suporte residencial com triagem rigorosa, pontualidade, paciência e linguagem acessível. Por que vai crescer: O cliente prateado quer continuar morando na própria casa (o chamado aging in place ), preservando sua independência sem precisar incomodar ninguém ou depender de favores. Não se vende apenas um parafuso apertado; mas autonomia, confiança e respeito ao tempo do cliente. Espaços de convivência e atividades: o antídoto contra o isolamento A solidão crônica tem impacto comparável ao tabagismo para a saúde. Quando a rotina de trabalho diminui e a casa fica vazia, a falta de convivência social precisa ser preenchida com propósito e pertencimento. O modelo de negócio: hubs urbanos diurnos, clubes de membros, centros de atividades culturais, tecnológicas e físicas, desenhados para acolher e promover trocas autênticas entre pares. Por que vai crescer: os modelos antigos de “asilo” ou centros de convivência assistenciais não conversam com o público moderno de 60, 70 ou 80 anos. Essa geração busca aprender programação básica, participar de debates, ter aulas de gastronomia, praticar atividades físicas e, acima de tudo, fazer novos amigos com interesses semelhantes. O valor está na experiência e na comunidade. Agências de viagem especializadas: da fuga do tédio à construção de histórias Viajar é um dos principais destinos dos recursos acumulados ao longo de décadas de trabalho. No entanto, o turismo convencional peca ao oscilar entre pacotes de aventura extrema ou excursões engessadas e apressadas. O modelo de negócio: roteiros de slow travel , viagens culturais em pequenos grupos, segurança logística refinada, acessibilidade sem estigma e experiências que equilibram conforto e vivência autêntica. Por que vai crescer: o tempo livre agora é abundante, mas a pressa acabou. Esse viajante não quer apenas “tirar fotos de pontos turísticos”; quer saborear a gastronomia local, caminhar no seu próprio ritmo, criar memórias e, muitas vezes, viajar desacompanhado com a segurança de um grupo com a mesma energia. É o combate direto ao tédio por meio do deslumbramento contínuo. Sexshop e intimidade: desmistificando o tabu do prazer e do autocuidado Talvez a maior miopia do mercado seja imaginar que o desejo, a curiosidade e a busca por afeto evaporam aos 60 anos. Com o aumento da expectativa de vida, tratamentos hormonais modernos e os novos arranjos de relacionamento (ou mesmo o redescobrimento da própria sexualidade após a viuvez ou o divórcio), a intimidade ganha outro significado. O modelo de negócio: marcas focadas em bem-estar íntimo, produtos ergonômicos, lubrificantes de alta performance, estimuladores sensoriais discretos e conteúdo educativo sem vulgaridade. Por que vai crescer: o envelhecimento moderno recusa a invisibilidade afetiva e sexual. Pequenas barreiras anatômicas ou hormonais podem ser facilmente superadas pela tecnologia e pela informação. articles.titleKo: Ministério do Trabalho registra 4,3 mil denúncias de assédio eleitoral em 3 dias; SP lidera
articles.originalSummary: O Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE) registrou 4.305 denúncias de assédio eleitoral no ambiente de trabalho entre a quarta-feira, 28, e a sexta-feira, 30. As notificações foram feitas nos três primeiros dias do funcionamento do canal criado para esse tipo de ocorrência. Os casos estão sob investigação da Auditoria Fiscal do Trabalho do MTE. O Sudeste é a região que apresenta o maior número de casos, com 2.087 denúncias. São Paulo lidera o ranking estadual, com 1.325 casos, seguido pelo Rio de Janeiro (354) e por Minas Gerais (345). Juntos, os três Estados somam 2.024 denúncias, o equivalente a 47% do total recebido pelo Ministério. O Paraná, com 268 denúncias, e Santa Catarina, com 259, completam o ranking. Na última semana, os boicotes a empresas e relatos de demissões motivados por posicionamentos políticos pautaram debates em todo o País. Nas redes sociais, trabalhadores relataram casos de demissão e temem sofrer retaliações após o resultado eleitoral. O assédio eleitoral acontece quando há ameaças ou outras formas de coação para influenciar o voto dos trabalhadores ou retaliação posterior pelo posicionamento político. Denúncias por unidade da Federação: São Paulo (SP): 1.325 Rio de Janeiro (RJ): 354 Minas Gerais (MG): 345 Paraná (PR): 268 Santa Catarina (SC): 259 Rio Grande do Sul (RS): 230 Ceará (CE): 172 Bahia (BA): 169 Goiás (GO): 143 Pernambuco (PE): 137 Pará (PA): 130 Maranhão (MA): 99 Mato Grosso (MT): 93 Distrito Federal (DF): 91 Espírito Santo (ES): 63 Rio Grande do Norte (RN): 63 Amazonas (AM): 52 Mato Grosso do Sul (MS): 51 Alagoas (AL): 50 Paraíba (PB): 42 Piauí (PI): 30 Acre (AC): 29 Rondônia (RO): 29 Amapá (AP): 25 Sergipe (SE): 22 Roraima (RR): 17 Tocantins (TO): 17 Sanções na Justiça e penas para empresas De acordo com o Código Eleitoral, os empregadores podem sofrer sanções na Justiça. “Não podemos admitir que trabalhadores e trabalhadoras sejam ameaçados, constrangidos ou discriminados por suas escolhas políticas”, disse o ministro do Trabalho e Emprego Luiz Marinho. “Nenhum empregador pode usar sua posição para interferir na decisão de seus empregados.” “O Governo do Brasil está atento às denúncias, atuando na fiscalização e adotando as providências necessárias para proteger os direitos dos trabalhadores”, afirma Marinho. As denúncias são realizadas por meio de um canal criado pelo MTE justamente para ouvir os trabalhadores que se sentirem prejudicados. Os relatos passam por análise e apuração para verificar a ocorrência de possíveis irregularidades e garantir a proteção dos trabalhadores e das trabalhadoras. De acordo com o secretário de Inspeção do Trabalho, Luiz Henrique, caso a situação seja confirmada, a instituição prevê adotar medidas administrativas e até dificultar o acesso a recursos financeiros. “Ao verificarmos a situação de assédio, de discriminação, a Fiscalização do Trabalho vai fazer a lavratura do auto de infração e também encaminhar essa informação aos órgãos públicos, ao Banco Central, para que haja essa proibição de financiamento e empréstimo”, afirma. O órgão também estuda criar uma ferramenta de transparência semelhante ao da lista de empregadores responsabilizados por trabalho análogo à escravidão. Combate ao assédio eleitoral Entre as medidas para prevenir e combater o assédio eleitoral no ambiente de trabalho, estão ações para retirar do ar sites e publicações nas redes sociais que incentivem a perseguição ou a discriminação por motivação política. As iniciativas incluem notificações a plataformas digitais, como Google e Meta, com base em orientação técnica da Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU). Além disso, os trabalhadores que utilizam a Carteira de Trabalho Digital estão recebendo mensagens com orientações sobre direitos e procedimentos para registrar denúncias. articles.title: 61-Unit Outback Steakhouse Franchisee Files for Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: 61-Unit Outback Steakhouse Franchisee Files for Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Out West Restaurant Group's financial troubles date back years. Outback Steakhouse franchisee Out West Restaurant Group filed for bankruptcy Monday, and parent company Bloomin’ Brands agreed to purchase substantially all of the operator’s assets through a court-supervised sale. Out West operates 61 Outback restaurants in the western U.S. The independently owned franchisee, formally known as Cerca Trova Restaurant Group Holdings, filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. Bloomin’ signed an asset purchase agreement Sunday with a starting purchase price of $26.3 million, subject to adjustments and the assumption of certain liabilities. The restaurant company also agreed to provide up to $5.5 million in interest-free financing to support Out West during the bankruptcy proceedings. The proposed financing would help Out West cover operating expenses and professional and administrative costs associated with the Chapter 11 case. Access would be allowed only when operating cash falls short of the minimum cash needed. During the bankruptcy process, Out West plans to continue paying newly incurred franchise fees and royalties owed to Bloomin’, along with rent under leases guaranteed by the company. Out West has had payment issues leading up to bankruptcy. In December 2023, Bloomin’, the franchisee, and its lenders reached an agreement to delay payments and hold off on enforcing certain rights tied to earlier defaults. Under that agreement, a bankruptcy filing would trigger repayment of amounts owed to Bloomin’ and substantial sums owed to lenders, with lenders getting paid first. However, instead, the bankruptcy filing put those provisions on hold, leaving the parties’ rights to be resolved in court. The filing does not immediately affect restaurant operations, according to Bloomin’. Out West plans to continue operating during the case and has requested court permission to pay certain employee, vendor, supplier, and other obligations incurred before its bankruptcy petitions. The proposed acquisition would give Bloomin’ Brands direct control of the franchisee’s restaurant assets if the transaction closes. The company said securing the restaurants would provide direct operational insight, allow investments through its development initiatives, and help limit disruption to guests and employees. The agreement positions Bloomin’ to become the stalking horse bidder, pending court approval. That role establishes an initial offer for the assets, but competing buyers can submit higher or otherwise better proposals through the bankruptcy sale process. An auction could follow if qualified competing bids emerge. Any sale to Bloomin’ requires court approval and satisfaction of other conditions in the purchase agreement. articles.title: The Margin Leak Hiding in Cleaners, Disposables, and Supplies
articles.titleKo: The Margin Leak Hiding in Cleaners, Disposables, and Supplies
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Non-food prices move like any other, but several habits let them move unnoticed. Full-service restaurant owners know their food cost closely. They know what the ribeye costs, when halibut spikes, and which produce supplier ran high last month. That attention is well placed, because food is the biggest purchasing line. But food is not the only thing a restaurant buys. Behind the line and around the dining room sits a second category: dish chemicals, sanitizers, gloves, to-go containers, napkins, liners, foil, parchment, and the smallwares and chef supplies that keep service running. It is bought on routine, rarely questioned, and rarely compared against the market. That makes it one of the quietest margin leaks in a full-service restaurant. The Spend Nobody Reviews A full-service operation buys an enormous range of non-food items. Each one is a small purchase, which is exactly why the category escapes scrutiny. A case of gloves or a drum of dish machine detergent does not feel like a decision. It is reordered because the last one ran out. Added together, those small purchases make up a real share of what a restaurant spends. Yet they rarely appear in the conversations about margin. Menu engineering focuses on plates, and purchasing reviews focus on proteins and produce. The supplies line gets whatever attention is left over, which is usually none. Why the Price Drifts Non-food prices move like any other, but several habits let them move unnoticed: Routine reordering. Items are ordered by habit from the same supplier, so no one asks whether the price is still competitive. Low per-unit cost. A few cents of difference on a single glove or container looks too small to chase, even when volume makes it significant. Many items, many suppliers. The same product may be sold by several vendors at different prices, and no one has time to line them up. No clear owner. Food has a chef or a kitchen manager watching it. Supplies often belong to whoever happens to place the order. None of this is carelessness. It is what happens when a category has hundreds of lines and no system that watches them. Why Looking Now and Then Doesn’t Solve It The usual fix is to look at a few supply prices occasionally. That helps a little, but it leaves most of the category untouched. The items that get checked are the ones someone remembered, while the rest keep drifting. A check is also only a snapshot. It reflects one day’s prices from the suppliers someone happened to ask, and it starts aging immediately. In a category with this many items, no one has the time to keep re-checking by hand. What Real-Time Price Comparison Changes The answer is to take the manual work out of it. When price comparison runs automatically and in real time across every item a restaurant buys, the supplies line gets the same scrutiny as the steak. That shift does several things: Every item is compared, not a sample. Dish chemicals, disposables and chef supplies are checked against the market alongside food, so nothing is left to routine. Price changes appear as they happen. The operator sees a movement when it occurs, not weeks later on an invoice. The work no longer depends on anyone’s time. A system that compares continuously does not skip a busy weekend or a staffing gap. Choices rest on current numbers. When it is time to reorder, the operator knows what the market looks like today. The result is not a new process for the team to follow. It is a layer of visibility that works in the background while the kitchen runs. articles.titleKo: Top Chefs: Where Are They in 2026?
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Competing on a show like Top Chef looks a lot like living inside a pressure cooker—and there are pros and cons to that, as one can imagine. The high-pressure environment is stressful, and forces chefs to quickly learn and adapt to survive. But they come out on the other end irrevocably changed in one way or another—whether it’s the practical lesson of knowing exactly what you can execute in 30 minutes, the reality of what national exposure does (and doesn’t) do for reservations, or the emotional shift that comes from turning a cast of competitors into a kind of restaurant-family for life. Charbel Hayek ( Top Chef Middle East & North Africa (MENA) Season 5 and Top Chef: World All-Stars ) puts it best: “The pressure will push you to move faster and make decisions in seconds, but you still need to trust your instincts, taste your food, and remember why you’re competing.” Across five former “cheftestants,” a few recurring themes emerged: the shift from solo talent to shared leadership and real teamwork, and the way that living under the clock sharpened their instincts, clarified their point of view, and taught them to treat every dish and every decision as intentional. In the stories and interviews that follow, they explain where Top Chef pushed them, what stuck, and how those lessons are shaping their decision-making today. What lingers in the end is a new way of thinking about food, leadership, and what it actually takes to run a restaurant in 2026. Scott Suchman Anthony Jones Season 23 Current role / title: Executive Chef, Marcus DC Anthony Jones is having a breakout year. Even before competing on the most recent season of Top Chef: Carolinas in Charlotte, which premiered in March 2026, Jones received a national recognition that many chefs only dream of. Back in late January, he remembers exercising in the gym at work when a friend texted him, “Congrats on the nom,” to which Jones replied, “What are you talking about?” His friend told him to go check Instagram—and that’s how Jones found out he was named a 2026 James Beard Award semifinalist for Emerging Chef. He stepped out of the room, feeling emotional. “That was a groundbreaking moment for me,” he says. “I will say, the gym is not the right place to shed tears. It makes everyone in the room with you feel a little uncomfortable,” he laughs. “So I had to pop out of there real quick. But I was beyond happy.” Before filming season 23 of Top Chef, Jones was helping celebrity chef Marcus Samuelsson launch Marcus DC inside The Morrow Hotel, which officially opened in D.C.’s Union Market District on June 3, 2025. Samuelsson tapped Jones to lead the kitchen as executive chef, where he has crafted a menu that reflects his upbringing in nearby Sunderland, Maryland, close to Chesapeake Bay. Mel’s Crab Rice, a mainstay on the Marcus DC menu, is a great example. Jones grew up cracking crabs with his family, and turned that childhood memory into one of DC’s most sought-after dishes: a mix of crunchy shallots, okra, obe, and uni-infused béarnaise. Scott Suchman In creating Mel’s Crab Rice, Jones “wanted to bring together my current self and my past self,” he says, but also acknowledges how much the dish has evolved over time. “I think we’re on iteration 12 or 13 of the rice since when we opened, because … I’m always adding something to it, changing up a step, adding in different flavor enhancers or ingredients, because I feel as though there’s always room for dishes to improve. For me, that’s the goal, especially for one of those dishes that has become iconic at the restaurant.” All his work has clearly paid off. Mel’s Crab Rice was named one of the best dishes in the city by The Washington Post, which also named Marcus DC a top five restaurant in the D.C. area. articles.title: Punch Bowl Social and Pinstripes to Launch Holiday Programming
articles.titleKo: Punch Bowl Social and Pinstripes to Launch Holiday Programming
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Both Punch Bowl Social and Pinstripes will host holiday menu “First Taste” events at all location. Punch Bowl Social has announced the return of its annual holiday programming – and with it, Pinstripes, which was acquired by the same parent company, joins in the fun. Festive and fun events, décor and specialty cocktails across all 11 Punch Bowl Socials and eight Pinstripes locations will launch Friday, Nov. 6. Additionally, both brands will launch festive pop-ups with the Dallas-based Ugly Christmas Sweater Shop, offering a selection of upcycled and new holiday garbs, across select locations. “We’ve loved seeing our collaboration with the Ugly Christmas Sweater Shop flourish over the years and are excited to introduce this activation to Pinstripes guests as well,” said Becki Howard, Punch Bowl Social’s senior director of programming. “Paired with the specialty cocktail menus and seasonal programming, Punch Bowl Social and Pinstripes will be the most festive spots in town.” Punch Bowl Social’s limited-edition holiday cocktail menu features five festive sips. The menu includes the Baked Apple Old Fashioned, with Jack Daniel’s Old No. 7 and a housemade baked apple reduction; Ho-Ho-Ho, a festive spin on an Irish coffee with Bacardi light rum, cold foam and a hint of spice; Peppermint Mocha Espresso Martini with Tito’s vodka and festive flavors, garnished with a mini candy cane; and a zero-proof Lychee Lemonade for a refreshing non-alcoholic sipper. Punch Bowl Social has also brought back Santa Pants, a holiday rendition of the mule made with Pantalones reposado tequila, playfully garnished with a miniature pair of Santa’s pants as a nod to the brand. Pinstripes will feature its own limited-time holiday menu, which includes a Chai Old Fashioned and Baked Apple Old Fashioned, both made with Jack Daniel’s Old No. 7; a refreshing Pomegranate Limoncello Spritz; two festive takes on a classic with a Chai Espresso Martini and Pumpkin Espresso Martini, each topped with a decadent Irish cream; and the Ginger Rose, a festive zero-proof offering. Both Punch Bowl Social and Pinstripes will host holiday menu “First Taste” events at all locations, during which guests can enjoy $2 off limited-edition holiday cocktails all day paired with signature games and dining offerings. In addition to the limited-time holiday menus, Punch Bowl Social and Pinstripes will serve as holiday cheer HQ with festive lineups of events across all locations. Punch Bowl Social guests can look forward to its weekly lineup of signature events like Karaoke, Music Bingo and Monday Funday. Pinstripes will also feature programming with festive spins throughout the season like their beloved Santa Brunch, every Saturday and Sunday from Nov. 28 through Dec. 20 at all locations. Both brands will introduce Drinksgiving on Wednesday, Nov. 25, for pre-Thanksgiving gatherings at select locations, and New Year’s Eve celebrations across all markets. The Ugly Christmas Sweater Shop pop-up will launch at select Punch Bowl Social and Pinstripes locations beginning early-November and run through Monday, Dec. 27 during regular business hours. Helping guests find the perfect fashions for every holiday occasion, The Ugly Sweater Shop pop-ups will feature an eclectic assortment of spirited upcycled and new holiday sweaters, ranging in price from $14.99 to $42.95. The Ugly Christmas Sweater Shop was founded by Dallas-based vintage clothing guru Jeremy Turner in 2013 after he noticed a demand for the iconic garments at his mobile vintage store. It took a multi-year hiatus during COVID and was relaunched at Punch Bowl Social Dallas in 2023. articles.title: Russo’s New York Pizzeria & Italian Kitchen Announces New Incentive to Spark Growth in Texas
articles.titleKo: Russo’s New York Pizzeria & Italian Kitchen Announces New Incentive to Spark Growth in Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Russo’s New York Pizzeria & Italian Kitchen, the Houston-founded pizza and Italian restaurant franchise, today announced a limited-time incentive for multi-unit developers in Texas: development agreements covering three or more Texas restaurants signed by December 31, 2026 will receive 50% off the initial franchise fee, reducing it from $35,000 to $17,500 per qualifying restaurant. The offer is part of a push to grow the brand’s Texas footprint, with Dallas–Fort Worth, Austin and additional Houston-area trade areas as priority markets. Russo’s operated 30 U.S. restaurants at the end of 2025, 24 of them franchised, with additional locations in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, and has signed development agreements for Sacramento, California and Mexico City. “Texas is where this brand was born and where we know the customer best,” said Chef Anthony Russo, founder and CEO of Russo’s New York Pizzeria. “We built this incentive for operators who want to open a group of restaurants, not just one. Lowering the entry cost on a three-store commitment is the fastest way we know to put the right owners in the right Texas markets.” Founded by Chef Russo in Houston in 1992 and franchising since 1998, Russo’s differs from carryout-focused pizza chains by operating a full-service Italian kitchen. Menus are built around hand-stretched New York-style pizza, house-made dough and sauces, house-made sausage, fresh pasta, lasagna and calzones, served through dine-in, takeout, delivery and catering. Restaurants typically occupy 1,800 to 3,500 square feet in suburban markets and lifestyle centers. According to Item 19 of the company’s 2026 Franchise Disclosure Document, the top 50% of U.S. franchised Russo’s restaurants averaged $1,042,444 in net sales in fiscal year 2025, and the top 25% averaged $1,368,586. These are historical net sales figures for 21 franchised restaurants open a full 12 months, not profit or owner income, and individual results vary. The Texas incentive applies to new development agreements for at least three Texas locations signed by December 31, 2026, with timely openings required. It is not available for single-unit agreements and cannot be combined with other offers unless approved in writing. Candidates must meet the brand’s standard qualifications, including $250,000 in liquid capital. Markets and territories are subject to availability and approval. Russo’s offers franchises in 36 states and Washington, D.C., with registrations pending in New York, Maryland and Hawaii, and reviews international developers on a case-by-case basis. Prospective franchisees can review the Texas offer, request the franchise kit or book a call with Franchise Development at russosfranchise.com/texas-franchise or by calling (832) 849-0724. articles.title: Thompson Restaurants Brings Back Meals with Meaning for Thanksgiving
articles.titleKo: Thompson Restaurants Brings Back Meals with Meaning for Thanksgiving
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . This Thanksgiving, Thompson Restaurants is making it easier to put a memorable meal on the table while giving guests the opportunity to do the same for a neighbor in need. Meals with Meaning returns this holiday season, giving guests the opportunity to donate complete, ready-to-serve Thanksgiving meals to local families facing food insecurity across the DMV. Each feast features holiday favorites from across the Thompson Restaurants family, helping make Thanksgiving a little brighter for families in need. From Nov. 1 through Dec. 31, guests can order a Thanksgiving feast for their own holiday table or give back through Meals with Meaning by donating a complete Thanksgiving meal to a local family in need. Guests can choose to provide a feast for a family of four for $100 or a meal for two for $50. Guests can also support the initiative by rounding up their checks at participating Thompson Restaurants. The program is made possible in partnership with the Northwest Federal Credit Union Foundation. Last Thanksgiving, Thompson Restaurants and its guests helped provide more than 1,100 meals to those in need through Meals with Meaning. This year, the restaurant group hopes to build on that impact and help even more families across the DMV share in the holiday season. “Thanksgiving is about coming together, and now more than ever, we need to support those in our community who need a helping hand,” said Alex Berentzen, COO of Thompson Restaurants. “Meals with Meaning gives our guests a simple way to enjoy Thanksgiving with their own families while helping another family do the same.” “Access to a nutritious meal can make a meaningful difference for families facing food insecurity, especially during the holiday season,” said Taralyn Tharp Kohler, Foundation Director of Northwest Federal Credit Union Foundation. “We’re grateful to continue our partnership with Thompson Restaurants and build on the incredible generosity we saw last year. Together, we hope to help even more of our neighbors gather around the table and enjoy a Thanksgiving meal this year.” For guests looking to take the stress out of Thanksgiving hosting, Meals with Meaning brings together holiday favorites from Matchbox, Milk & Honey, Makers Union and Ms. Peach’s in two complete feast options: Classic Feast | $155 Choice of Oven-Roasted Turkey Breast or Glazed Ham, homemade gravy, traditional cranberry sauce, biscuits or cornbread and a choice of three sides: Matchbox Mashed Potatoes Matchbox Garlic & Herb Stuffing Matchbox Honey Glazed Carrots Milk & Honey Mac & Cheese Milk & Honey Collard Greens Milk & Honey Yams Makers Union Brussels Sprouts Makers Union Garlic Green Beans Deluxe Feast | $185 Everything included in the Classic Feast, plus one additional side and a choice of dessert: Ms. Peach’s Pecan Pie, Pumpkin Pie or Apple Pie. Guests can also complete their table with additional sides for $20 each and additional desserts for $25 each. All feasts serve 4–6 people and include tax. Customers are encouraged to place their Thanksgiving feast orders online by Friday, November 20 at 12 p.m., with meal pick-up scheduled for Wednesday, November 25. Customers can visit www.thompsonrestaurants.com/thanksgiving-2026 to select their preferred feast or donate a meal. For those looking to dine out on Thanksgiving Day, L’Auberge Chez Francios, The Delegate, Ridley and Hen Quarter Prime will be open. For more information or to make reservations, visit thompsonrestaurants.com. The post Thompson Restaurants Brings Back Meals with Meaning for Thanksgiving appeared first on FSR magazine .

The launch builds on a year of significant menu innovation for Ojos Locos. Ojos Locos Sports Cantina is continuing its culinary evolution with the introduction of Chicharrones con Guacamole, the latest addition to its growing lineup of authentic Latin-inspired dishes. Inspired by the traditional chicharrón con carne found at Mexican carnicerías, the new dish features crispy, meaty pieces of fried pork belly. It’s served with a generous portion of house-made guacamole topped with pico de gallo, alongside salsa roja, salsa verde and corn tortillas made by hand daily at every Ojos Locos cantina. The launch builds on a year of significant menu innovation for Ojos Locos. In 2026, the brand has introduced an expanded lineup of dishes without removing longtime favorites. Recent additions include Carne Asada, Cali Burrito, Burrito Bowl, Carne Asada Fries, Birria Pizza, Birria Ramen, Mexicali Shrimp Tacos, Guajillo Wing Rub, and a revamped Smash Burger, along with breakfast offerings like Chilaquiles Rojos o Verdes. Led by corporate Chef Alex Sadowsky, Vice President of Training, Culinary & Beverage, the menu expansion reflects Ojos’ renewed focus on its scratch kitchen, bringing new flavors and more variety to guests while staying true to its Latin roots.
